Super Mario! Dons hand rebuild job to Swiss success story Frick

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their newly introduced head coach.
  • The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026.

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their newly introduced head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

Sources indicate that frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington said the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington said: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

It has been revealed that 'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'.

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

Sources indicate that pfannenstiel said: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their newly introduced manager.

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'.

Before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

According to recent reports, as a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

Frick remarked: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and significant ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'.

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

Arsenal, Tottenham 'told to pay £70m' for Championship star

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 20:01.
  • Arsenal are reportedly interested in signing Will Lankshear during the January transfer window, but Middlesbrough have no intention of letting their prized striker leave.
  • The Gunners have been linked with a move for the 21-year-old, who has been in sensational goalscoring form for Boro this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 20:01.

Arsenal are reportedly interested in signing Will Lankshear during the January transfer window, but Middlesbrough have no intention of letting their prized striker leave.

The Gunners have been linked with a move for the 21-year-old, who has been in sensational goalscoring form for Boro this season.

Lankshear joined the Riverside outfit from Tottenham Hotspur for £20m during the summer transfer window and wasted little time establishing himself as one of their key players.

The young striker has scored 15 goals in 16 appearances for Boro, helping the Teessiders climb to second in the Championship table, level on points with Birmingham City and Stoke City.

According to The Sun, Boro are determined to resist any bids for Lankshear and have slapped a £70m price tag on the striker.

If Boro secure promotion to the Premier League next season, they could stand to make more than double the fee they paid for him, meaning a January sale would make little financial sense.

Leeds United and Newcastle United have also reportedly watched him in action this season, while Spurs are keeping a close eye on his development.

Tottenham do not have a buy-back clause in Lankshear's contract, as such clauses are not permitted in transfers between Premier League and EFL clubs.

However, the North London club do have matching rights, meaning they can match any offer another club has agreed with Middlesbrough for the striker in the future.

Mikel Arteta could be looking to bring in a new striker in January after Arsenal failed to land their top target, Julian Alvarez, during the summer window.

Viktor Gyokeres has managed just one Premier League start this season and has cut a somewhat subdued figure, struggling to make a significant impact so far.

The Gunners are also looking to strengthen their wide attacking options, with RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa heavily linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium.

While Lankshear is enjoying a fabulous campaign, it would make sense for Arsenal to assess his progress over a full season rather than spend a sizeable sum to secure his services in January.

Last night, AC Milan will have been very happy to see Christian Pulisic extending his fine goalscoring form with a brace for America.

Sources indicate that the United States national team have certainly faced a rocky few days. Thanks to Manchester United parting ways with Michael Carrick, Mauricio Pochettino will leave his role as the head coach of the project after the international break, leaving them in a strange position at the moment.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, however, that was not a problem for The Stars and The Stripes, who put six past Haiti in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League. Of course, who else would be key but Pulisic himself?

Playing as a number 10 in a 4-2-3-1 system – which will have pleased Milan’s coach, Ruben Amorim – Pulisic was instrumental, scoring a brace in just two minutes. After 62 minutes, he stepped up from the spot after drawing the penalty himself.

Then, just a minute later, he added a second and recorded his 35th goal for the USMNT in 91 appearances.

For the attacker, it extends his fine run of form and the second half of 2026 is proving to be much more fruitful than the first. In Serie A, he’s scored four goals and provided an assist in eight games, and he’s now grabbed two more for the national team. After missing the last camp, it’s another reminder of his importance.

With Pochettino departing, it’s clear that they’ll still be in fine hands, with Pulisic remaining key!

Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
  • By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.
  • Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Sources indicate that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

Sources indicate that the supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

Industry observers note that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

According to recent reports, equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

Industry observers note that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

According to recent reports, “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager remarked. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

In a recent development, it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Sources indicate that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

Sources indicate that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

In a recent development, spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Industry observers note that it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

Industry observers note that “But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

It has been revealed that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

According to recent reports, 3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu.

Industry observers note that the Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

Industry observers note that “We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

More jeers at the final whistle from United fans - they weren’t happy with this point against a team there for the taking after Rodrigo Bentancur’s dismissal. Michael Carrick is still trying to find answers because this United team is not clicking.

The late chaos is over at Old Trafford as Solanke rescues a precious point for Tottenham with that 92nd minute equaliser. Man Utd thought they had the game wrapped up after Mbeumo’s well-taken opener was followed by Bentancur’s crazy red card. However, Spurs, who were the better team throughout the contest, kept fighting and found a fully deserved leveller. The visitors remain winless, but it’s another worrying performance from Carrick’s side, who have picked up just one victory in six top-flight matches.

A point apiece in Manchester. https://t.co/xiEiQsFsje.

Dalot and Gray are both handed yellow cards for fouls that broke up play. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Spurs right now look like the more likely side to claim a victory.

It’s just the Spurs fans singing in Old Trafford now. They fully deserved that equaliser. Rashford and Heaven are on for the hosts, with Cunha and Shaw taken off.

Industry observers note that incredible drama at Old Trafford! Tonali floats a cross into the box and Solanke shrugs off Martinez, before flicking a delicate header into the bottom corner to send Spurs’ away support wild. Man Utd are stunned. Could the visitors go on and win this now?

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Van Hecke does well to block Cunha’s effort and the referee indicates that there will be a minimum of eight minutes of added time.

De Zerbi’s final roll of the dice in search of a late leveller sees Fernandes replace Senesi for the remaining few minutes. Spurs must throw everyone forward now.

Industry observers note that martinez lunges in on Maddison and brings down the playmaker with a foul. The centre-back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

In a recent development, baleba unleashes Mbeumo with an over-the-top through ball. Racing through on goal, the forward shoots, but from an unfavourable angle, Kinsky parries his near post effort out for a corner.

Fernandes is cautioned after catching Van Hecke with a late challenge on his ankle. Spurs players aren’t happy with the tackle.

Bentancur’s recklessness has left Spurs with a mountain to climb. Their chance of a comeback looks a bit slimmer now that Man Utd have a numerical advantage on the pitch.

It’s all kicked off at Old Trafford! Bentancur flies in with a risky challenge on Shaw. The Man Utd defender is furious with the tackle and the two players square up to each other. Recent findings suggest that zirkzee turns Senesi and threads a pass through to Fernandes. From a tight angle, the Man Utd captain slices a ferocious effort into the side netting. The playmaker has been quiet today, but you can never write him off from scoring or providing an assist.

Baleba’s first action in a Man Utd shirt sees the midfielder smash a hopeful volley wildly off target. Can Baleba’s introductrion lift the crowd and help give the hosts some impetus?

Industry observers note that you can feel the nervousness in the Old Trafford crowd. Spurs’ dominance has calmed over the last 10 minutes, but Man Utd have failed to take control or pick up the tempo.

Man Utd’s slow start prompts some boos from the home fans. Cunha attempts to rally the crowd, but his side have given their supporters nothing to be positive about in this game so far. Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Industry observers note that man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after big-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

According to recent reports, all eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

Latest Update: Gustavo Nunes, Kevin, Vitor Reis and Rodrigo Muniz fight for playing time in the Premier League

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (991 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 15 Nov 2026 20:06.
  • It has been revealed that four Brazilians are fighting for game time at the start of the 2026-27 Premier League season: Gustavo Nunes at Brentford, Kevin and Rodrigo Muniz at Fulham, and Vitor Reis at Manchester City.
  • It has been revealed that the Brazilian presence in the Premier League is not limited to the players who regularly appear among the standout names.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 15 Nov 2026 20:06.

It has been revealed that four Brazilians are fighting for game time at the start of the 2026-27 Premier League season: Gustavo Nunes at Brentford, Kevin and Rodrigo Muniz at Fulham, and Vitor Reis at Manchester City. They are young players seeking to establish themselves and a centre-forward trying to regain his prominence in England.

It has been revealed that the Brazilian presence in the Premier League is not limited to the players who regularly appear among the standout names. Alongside those who have won a place and become protagonists in England, there are also those trying to turn occasional chances into a longer run of games. None of the four has yet established himself among his manager’s main options, although for different reasons and in different circumstances. Some have barely featured in league games, while others have been used during matches but without enough time to build a run.

According to recent reports, gustavo Nunes joined Brentford in August 2024 after catching the eye at Gremio. Developed in the Brazilian club’s youth system, the forward made his professional debut in February that year and quickly earned a place. He played 40 games for the first team, scoring seven goals and providing four assists, numbers that helped attract English interest.

The move did not have the expected start. Physical problems delayed his debut for Brentford, who were only able to use him for the first time in April 2025. That season, he made three Premier League appearances, always from the bench, and had few opportunities to show his qualities.

Sources indicate that the search for more minutes led the club to loan him to Swansea City in January 2026. In the Championship, he played 12 games and provided one assist. After returning to Brentford, he rejoined the squad but has still not played in a Premier League game in 2026-27, alternating between being left out of the squad and being an unused substitute. At 20, he is trying to find a place in an attack where he still has to win the trust of boss Keith Andrews.

In a recent development, kevin, a Fulham forward, is another Brazilian looking for a bigger role. Developed at Palmeiras, he played for Shakhtar Donetsk before moving to the Premier League. In Ukraine, he stood out for his dribbling and attacking involvement, with 17 goals and 10 assists in 57 games between 2024 and 2025.

According to recent reports, fulham signed him in September 2025. In his first season in England, Kevin had opportunities throughout the campaign but did not establish himself as a starter. He made 26 Premier League appearances, nine of them as a starter, with one goal and two assists. In the early weeks of 2026-27, however, his involvement has shrunk. He has played five times in the league, always as a substitute, for only 75 minutes. In the EFL Cup, he was used in all three games for the Cottagers, two as a starter. Without a goal or assist so far, the 23-year-old is trying to use the minutes he gets to show he can be a more frequent alternative in Fulham’s attack.

It has been revealed that rodrigo Muniz has the most established record in the Premier League of the four. Signed by Fulham in August 2021 after a spell at Flamengo, the centre-forward needed time to adapt to English football. Before winning a place in the London side, he was loaned to Middlesbrough, for whom he played 17 games and scored two goals in the Championship.

His first big moment at Fulham came in 2023-24, when he scored nine goals in 26 Premier League games, 18 of them as a starter, and ten goals in 33 matches in all competitions. The following year he kept an crucial role, with eight goals in 31 top-flight games, only eight as a starter, and 11 goals in 36 matches across all competitions. In 2025-26, however, his numbers dropped sharply due to muscle injuries: 25 appearances and only one goal.

Sources indicate that the trend of reduced use continues this season. Muniz has played in eight Premier League games, all from the bench, for 96 minutes. Despite the limited space, he scored against Newcastle United on 7 November, his first goal of the current Premier League campaign and the third of the year, as he has also scored twice in the EFL Cup. At 25, the centre-forward is trying to use that kind of opportunity to regain ground in the battle to lead the attack.

Industry observers note that vitor Reis’ situation is slightly different. Signed by Manchester City in January 2025 after impressing at Palmeiras, the centre-back arrived in England with the status of one of the leading prospects in Brazilian defending. The investment by the English club reinforced expectations around his development, but competition for a place in the defensive system has always been an obstacle.

In the first half of 2025, he had very limited involvement before being loaned to Girona for the following season. In Spain, he found the space needed to gain experience in one of Europe’s top leagues. He played 36 La Liga games, with more than 3,000 minutes on the pitch, and scored one goal and provided one assist.

In a recent development, his return to Manchester City, however, did not bring an immediate change in outlook. In this Premier League season, Reis has made just one appearance, playing one minute off the bench. He has been given opportunities in other competitions, such as the EFL Cup (two full starts and one goal) and the Champions League (18 minutes against AEK Athens), but is still far from a run of games in the league. At 20, the centre-back is still adapting to the demands of English football and trying to turn the experience gained in Spain into a place in boss Enzo Maresca’s squad.

Things could’ve been much different for Paolo Maldini at AC Milan without two major figures in his life and career.

Industry observers note that maldini has two faces at Milan, but both remain adored by the fanbase. Firstly, you have the legendary defender, whose number was retired with him, a sign of respect and a chance to honour a career and legacy which surpasses many in the game.

According to recent reports, then, he returned as the sporting director, ending the Scudetto drought. Of course, that story didn’t have an ending as romantic as his playing career, but his legacy lives on. In fact, he may be voted into the Hall of Fame in the very near future.

Speaking to Tuttomercatoweb, via PianetaMilan, Maldini looked at the earliest stages of his career, as well as when he really took off for the Rossoneri.

“When my father took me to try out for AC Milan, I liked playing goalkeeper, but luckily I ended up choosing to be a defender. I played football with my friends in the park and at the youth club: I didn’t feel like I was destined for success at all, and until the day I made my debut, I never thought I could reach the highest levels.

“My dad always told me that the most important thing is to have fun, because if you treat it only as a job, it loses its magic.”.

“There’s one person in particular who believed in me and wanted me to play when I was 15: Nils Liedholm, then AC Milan’s coach. He loved showing his faith in young players, and once, during a break, he asked me whether I preferred to play on the right or left. I replied that it was obviously his choice, but it was a gesture that helped me a lot.”.

As they say, one change and the rest is history. With Maldini, that was certainly the case.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 15 Nov 2026 20:23.
  • Sources indicate that paris Saint-Germain are reportedly prepared to compete with Barcelona for a Premier League defender the Catalan club dream of lining up in central defence alongside Pau Cubarsi.
  • It has been revealed that it is no secret that Barcelona want to use the January transfer window to sign a fresh centre-back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 15 Nov 2026 20:23.

Sources indicate that paris Saint-Germain are reportedly prepared to compete with Barcelona for a Premier League defender the Catalan club dream of lining up in central defence alongside Pau Cubarsi. According to El Nacional, that defender is Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol.

It has been revealed that it is no secret that Barcelona want to use the January transfer window to sign a fresh centre-back. Germany international Jonathan Tah, whom Bayern Munich have no intention of losing, is no longer an option, but the Catalan hierarchy have activated other profiles. Hansi Flick’s side have also positioned themselves for Gvardiol.

According to recent reports, able to play in central defence, the Croatia international is most often used as a left-back by boss Enzo Maresca. Across the Premier League and the Champions League, the 24-year-old has started nine times in that position since the beginning of 2026-27. But it is for central defence that Barcelona are thinking strongly about his arrival, with an improbable chance of success as early as January 2027.

Recent findings suggest that according to El Nacional, the proposal is to make him a future ‘ideal partner’ for Cubarsi, in an area where Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen are options with limited time left. Barcelona will have to convince Manchester City to sell a player of this calibre, who has a contract until 2031 and a reported market value of around £64m.

Another obstacle for Barcelona is fierce competition from other European powers. According to the same source, PSG, Liverpool, Bayern Munich and Chelsea are also interested in the former Dinamo Zagreb player.

Like their illustrious rivals, the French capital club are closely monitoring possible sanctions against Manchester City, who are threatened with relegation because of their financial irregularities and who, if such a sentence is confirmed, could be forced to sell all of their leading players.

Industry observers note that PSG’s reported interest runs into two questions, however. Until proven otherwise, the double Champions League holders are not prioritising a left-back, preferring a right-sided centre-back and a right-back to back up Achraf Hakimi.

Gvardiol may also be more tempted by a challenge at Barcelona, in a squad where competition looks less fierce than at PSG, with Willian Pacho in central defence and Nuno Mendes on the left.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The number of men with high citation counts exceeds that of women.Credit: FotografiaBasica/iStock via Getty.

Women are more frequently mentioned in the acknowledgements section of papers than credited as co-authors, especially for research and analytical work, a study has found. But status seems to trump gender.

An analysis of more than 20,000 authors and 60,000 acknowledged contributors on papers published in seven PLOS journals between 2016 and 2021 highlighted persistent disparities between women and men in who gets authorship over an acknowledgement.

The study, published in Scientometrics1, also found that highly cited researchers — used by the authors as a proxy for higher status — were more likely to receive authorship over acknowledgement than were their less-cited collaborators, irrespective of gender. When a highly cited woman collaborated with a less-cited man, for example, the woman was more likely to be credited as an author.

It has been revealed that authorship is one of the most crucial metrics in research evaluation, grant reviews and promotion decisions, whereas acknowledgements aren’t typically factored in. The difference between getting authorship credit versus an acknowledgement can make or break a researcher’s career. One famous example is chemist Rosalind Franklin, a key contributor to the discovery of the DNA double helix. Franklin was mentioned in the acknowledgements section of the 1953 paper describing the finding, which went on to win the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, rather than being named a co-author with James Watson and Francis Crick.

In a recent development, the Scientometrics study highlights the importance of status in determining who gets credit, and the uphill battle that many women in research have to face — especially in their early and mid-careers. The number of highly cited men exceeded that of women, suggesting that even if women benefit from high status once they have attained it, fewer women attain higher status in the first place.

“We realized that the issue is double. One linked with gender bias, but another surprisingly due to hierarchy bias,” notes Yukie Sano, a computational scientist at the University of Tsukuba in Japan, who co-authored the paper.

The impact of a researcher’s status and gender on academic credit is well-documented, but Sano and her co-authors point to the Contributor Role Taxonomy (CRediT) — a standardized system describing specific roles that individual scientists often take on during research — as a game-changer by providing high-quality data to track this metric across journals and disciplines.

In a recent development, sano and her colleagues used CRediT data from open-access PLOS journals (which implemented the system in 2016) to track the contributions of authors and devised a separate system to track contributions in the acknowledgements section. Author gender was determined using Gender API, an artificial-intelligence-powered service that infers a person’s gender on the basis of their name.

It has been revealed that the team found that men were generally more likely than women to receive authorship credit — particularly in investigation roles (performing the experiments) and analysis roles (analysing or synthesizing the study data). Around 70% of men were credited as authors, compared with about 65% of women.

The size of the gender gap varied between disciplines, but was particularly evident in medicine, biology and computer science, whereas environmental science indicated little evidence of a gender difference in authorship versus acknowledgement rates.

Real Madrid transfer news: Fabrizio Romano reveals truth behind Trent Alexander-Arnold to Liverpool links

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 20:31.
  • Trent Alexander-Arnold has struggled to secure regular game time at Real Madrid this season, but a return to Liverpool in January appears to be out of the question.
  • The 28-year-old joined Madrid from Liverpool in the summer of 2025 and has made 43 appearances for the Spanish giants across all competitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 20:31.

Trent Alexander-Arnold has struggled to secure regular game time at Real Madrid this season, but a return to Liverpool in January appears to be out of the question.

The 28-year-old joined Madrid from Liverpool in the summer of 2025 and has made 43 appearances for the Spanish giants across all competitions.

However, the England international has managed just four starts in La Liga this season, with a further three appearances coming off the bench.

Alexander-Arnold has lost his place to Federico Valverde, with Jose Mourinho preferring to deploy the midfielder at right-back ahead of two recognised full-backs.

This has fuelled speculation that a potential return to Liverpool could be on the cards, but Fabrizio Romano has poured cold water on those rumours.

Romano has dismissed suggestions that all three parties are involved in discussions over a potential transfer.

Alexander-Arnold rose through Liverpool's academy to establish himself as one of the best right-backs in world football, although his departure from Anfield was not universally well received.

"Let’s immediately clarify one thing, there is zero ongoing between Trent Alexander-Arnold, Real Madrid and Liverpool, zero at all," mentioned Romano to DAZN Football, as relayed by Roundtable.

The Italian journalist further emphasised that, while Alexander-Arnold retains enormous affection for the Reds, his priorities remain firmly in the Spanish capital.

According to recent reports, "Trent obviously respects and loves the club but that’s it, it’s in the past. Trent is fully focused on Real Madrid and there is no contact or negotiation at all with Liverpool.".

The England right-back would have been a fantastic addition to Andoni Iraola's system, but it appears unlikely that the Reds have any intends to bring him back.

Jeremie Frimpong has struggled to make a significant impact, but Ronald Araujo, who joined on loan from Barcelona, has done a decent job at right-back so far.

Conor Bradley remains sidelined through injury and is unlikely to return before the end of the year, but bringing in another right-back is not at the moment a top priority for Liverpool.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:49 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 15 November 2026.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

Bacher, 30, essentially failed to let go of the ball at the right time, leaving his team-mates stunned.

The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

According to recent reports, arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

"Están matando al fútbol"Por el "insólito" gol en contra que se hace el arquero de Comunicaciones ante Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/GLUJlcKPXK.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored a bizarre own goal during his side's third-tier play-off game.

The 30-year-old failed to release the ball from a throw and launched the ball into his own net.

Fans flooded to social media to react to the scarcely believable own goal.

Sources indicate that one wrote on X: 'Haha, those who think it's because of betting. That's the level of Argentine football.'.

Another posted: 'RIP Argentinian football.'.

According to recent reports, A third shared: 'The Arsenal lot celebrating... you've got some nerve.'.

Bacher joined the club at the start of last year, but has always played in his homeland of Argentina.

His Comunicaciones side finished ninth in their league group of Primera B, the third tier of Argentinian football, and were taken on by an Arsenal side that came second.

They will face off in the return leg next Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42.
  • Tunisia will be looking to repair their faltering Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they travel to the 11 June Stadium in Tripoli to face Libya on Tuesday.
  • The Mediterranean Knights moved onto four points from three Group H matches with Friday's victory in Sfax, while the Eagles of Carthage sit bottom of the table with two points, still waiting for their first win of the campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42.

Tunisia will be looking to repair their faltering Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they travel to the 11 June Stadium in Tripoli to face Libya on Tuesday.

The Mediterranean Knights moved onto four points from three Group H matches with Friday's victory in Sfax, while the Eagles of Carthage sit bottom of the table with two points, still waiting for their first win of the campaign.

Libya opened their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-2 draw at home to Botswana, coming from two goals down through Marwan Al-Habashi's strike in the 87th minute and Ezoo El Mariamy's penalty deep into stoppage time.

They then suffered a 1-0 defeat away to Uganda, with Arnold Vula scoring the only goal, leaving them bottom of Group H before Friday's result moved them towards the top end of the table.

Coach Youssouph Dabo, the Senegalese who replaced Ali Cisse, had not won a competitive match in charge before Friday, making the victory all the more significant.

In Sfax, Libya took the lead after Ali Maaloul fouled Muaid Issa in the box, allowing Ali Youssef to convert from the penalty spot in the 44th minute, before Hamdou El Houni doubled their advantage on the counter-attack shortly after the hour mark.

The result marked Tunisia's heaviest home defeat in AFCON qualifying and the first time they had trailed by two goals on home soil in the competition.

It also ended more than 25 years without a two-goal home defeat in the qualifiers, prompting angry supporters to throw bottles and set off flares, while players and staff confronted referee Hamza El Fariq, who was subsequently escorted from the stadium.

Coach Mouine Chaabani has since apologised to supporters and admitted that the defeat was deserved, although Tunisia's decline stretches further back than the current qualifying campaign.

They lost all three matches at the 2026 World Cup, suffering defeats against Sweden (5-1), Japan (4-0) and the Netherlands (3-1), and have now gone nine games without a win, including September's draws against Uganda (1-1) and Botswana (2-2).

Before this campaign, Tunisia had qualified for each of the last 17 AFCON finals, the longest active streak of any nation, but with only one team besides co-hosts Uganda able to progress from Group H, they are running out of room for error.

Their record against Libya remains encouraging, however, as the visitors had won the previous six meetings before Friday's encounter, including a 5-2 away victory in 2021 and 3-0 and 1-0 wins in 2023.

Libya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Tunisia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Tunisia form (all competitions):.

Libya are expected to rely heavily on home-based players from clubs in Tripoli and Benghazi, with Youssouph Dabo naming a 27-man squad for the double-header.

Al Hilal Benghazi forward Ezoo El Mariamy is among the main attacking options, while Hamdou El Houni will be hoping to recover from the injury that forced him off during the first leg after scoring.

Tunisia have also named a 27-man squad built around experienced internationals Ferjani Sassi, Aissa Laidouni, Ali Maaloul and Montassar Talbi, while Moetez Zemzemi and Mohamed Ali Ben Hammouda are among the new additions.

Elias Achouri was ruled out through injury before the first leg and has not been included in the squad for the trip to Libya.

Libya possible starting lineup:.

Al-Tihar; Jaddour, Elfadli, Musrati, Salama; Al-Shuraimi, Al-Hbeishi; Eissa, Ellafi, Tajouri; El Maremi.

Tunisia possible starting lineup:.

Dahmen; Ghram, Talbi, Maaloul; Drager, Laidouni, Ben Romdhane, Gharbi; Letaief, Saad; Chaouat.

Tunisia desperately need a victory, but they have scored just three goals in three qualifiers while conceding five, and Libya showed how dangerous they can be on the counter-attack in Sfax, with another positive result likely to leave the hosts in a strong position.

The visitors should be more assertive away from the pressure of their own supporters and possess greater individual quality, but their recent struggles suggest they could again enjoy plenty of possession without creating enough clear-cut opportunities.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42.
  • Niger will be looking to respond to their heavy defeat in the first meeting when they face Morocco again in Tuesday's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixture at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat.
  • The Mena suffered a 5-1 defeat in Casablanca on Friday, leaving them with three points from three Group A matches, while the Atlas Lions maintained their perfect start to the campaign and moved onto nine points after winning all three of their qualifiers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42.

Niger will be looking to respond to their heavy defeat in the first meeting when they face Morocco again in Tuesday's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixture at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat.

The Mena suffered a 5-1 defeat in Casablanca on Friday, leaving them with three points from three Group A matches, while the Atlas Lions maintained their perfect start to the campaign and moved onto nine points after winning all three of their qualifiers.

Niger began their qualifying campaign with a 2-1 victory over Lesotho, but they were unable to build on that result when they travelled to face Gabon, suffering a 2-0 defeat in their second Group A fixture.

They then lost by the same scoreline to Algeria in an international friendly in October, before Friday's 5-1 defeat against Morocco extended their losing run to three matches across all competitions.

Their latest defeat was particularly frustrating because they managed to reduce the deficit to 2-1 before half-time through Mohamed Abdouramane's header, and were handed an opportunity to equalise shortly afterwards when a penalty was awarded for a handball by Noussair Mazraoui.

However, Yassine Bounou saved Ousseini Badamassi's spot kick, and Achraf Hakimi restored Morocco's two-goal advantage with a free kick in first-half stoppage time before the Atlas Lions added two more goals after the break.

The Mena have now conceded nine goals in their last three outings, including a 2-1 friendly defeat to Algeria, while scoring just twice during that period, leaving coach Nabil Neghiz with plenty to address after a difficult start to his tenure.

Morocco have now scored nine goals and conceded just once in their opening three qualifiers, having started the campaign with consecutive 2-0 victories over Gabon and Lesotho before Friday's emphatic win.

The Atlas Lions also drew 1-1 with Mali in a friendly in October, but their competitive form has been considerably more impressive, with the latest result extending their winning run in AFCON qualifying to nine matches.

Morocco have also won their last 16 home matches in major tournament qualifiers, covering both the Africa Cup of Nations and World Cup, marking their longest-ever winning streak on home soil in such fixtures.

With Tuesday's match also taking place in Morocco, with Rabat serving as Niger's adopted home for this fixture, Mohamed Ouahbi's side will remain on familiar territory and look to make further use of that advantage.

Morocco have consequently won the last three encounters between the sides by an aggregate score of 12-2 and boast a perfect record in this fixture, having won all seven meetings across all competitions.

Niger Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Morocco Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Morocco form (all competitions):.

Niger named a 25-man squad for the November double-header, with nine players based in the domestic league and the rest drawn from clubs in Europe, Asia and other African countries.

Rahim Alhassane, who plays for Bologna, is expected to remain an important figure in defence, while Oumar Sako, Ali Mohamed, Daniel Sosah and experienced winger Tidjani Amadou Moutari are among the other notable selections.

Morocco are also working with the 26-man squad named by Ouahbi for the two matches, although several established internationals are missing, including Ismael Saibari, Azzedine Ounahi, Ayoub El Kaabi, Soufiane Rahimi, Chadi Riad and Hamza Igamane.

Youssef En-Nesyri returned to the squad and scored after coming off the bench in the first meeting, while Ayoub Oufkir marked his first senior call-up with a late goal, with both forwards now hoping to earn starting places after their contributions in Casablanca.

Niger possible starting lineup:.

Tanja; Camara, Sako, Abdouramane, Alhassane; Oumarou; Moutari, Ali Mohamed, Badamassi, Amoustapha; Sosah.

Morocco possible starting lineup:.

Bounou; Hakimi, Diop, Aguerd, Mazraoui; Bouaddi, Targhalline; Diaz, El Khannouss, Ezzalzouli; Zabiri.

Morocco have already demonstrated the gulf in quality between the sides, scoring five goals in Friday's meeting and extending their winning run in this fixture.

Niger have conceded nine goals in their last three games, and their inability to defend consistently makes it difficult to see them preventing another defeat against the Group A leaders.

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 21:48, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 22:02.

England inflicted Spain's first defeat in 43 games on the World Cup winners with a sensational 3-2 victory in the Nations League, thus progressing to the quarter-finals as group winners.

Evidently learning their lessons from their gut-wrenching World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, the Three Lions exploded out of the blocks in the Spanish capital, but Luis de la Fuente's backline weathered the early storm.

The world champions soon began to threaten James Trafford's goal too, but England got the reward their endeavours warranted on the stroke of the break, as Harry Kane dispatched a controversial penalty.

Neither the home nor away fans could then comprehend what they witnessed inside the opening 15 minutes of the second half, as Arsenal duo Ezri Konsa and Ben White incredibly extended England's lead, but the visitors were then forced to strap in for a nail-biting ending.

Barely moments after England's third went in, Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul and Mikel Oyarzabal dispatched the resulting penalty, before an Anthony Gordon error ended with Nico Williams cutting the arrears further.

However, the 10 men of England heroically held out in the dying embers to condemn Spain to their first loss since March 2024, and usurp the world and European champions at the top of League A Group 3.

De la Fuente's hitherto perfect troops could not live with England's intensity, pressing and sheer will to win, which they only matched when their visitors went down to 10 men - never before.

Spain also needed two individual mistakes from England to earn their route back into the game, but when the Three Lions maintained their discipline, the best in the world had no answers.

Scotland end their Nations League campaign with a clash against Switzerland on Monday, with their slim hopes of qualifying for the promotion playoffs still intact.

Placed in Group B1 alongside Slovenia, North Macedonia and the aforementioned Switzerland, new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli kept alive Scotland’s chances of claiming second spot in the group with a narrow 2-1 home win over North Macedonia on Friday, thanks to two goals from John McGinn.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Here’s what Scotland needs to happen to nab a promotion/relegation playoff spot, how to watch the draw and what a third-placed finish would mean for Pocognoli’s men.

First and foremost, Scotland MUST beat Switzerland to stand any chance of finishing in second place in the group. Should they achieve that, they will also have to hope Slovenia fail to beat North Macedonia. If Slovenia beat North Macedonia this evening, it is impossible for Scotland to finish in second place regardless of their result against Switzerland.

In the scenario that Scotland draw with Switzerland, and Slovenia lose to North Macedonia, both sides would be level on eight points. However, Slovenia would take second place following their 2-1 win at Hampden Park last month, with UEFA prioritizing head-to-head results between tied teams rather than overall goal difference. At the moment in third place on seven points, they trail Slovenia in second place on eight points.

Sources indicate that the draw for the Nations League playoffs will take place on Friday, 20 November. The draw begins at 11am UK time and will take place at UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

You can stream the draw live via your smart TV, laptop, tablet or mobile phone, the entire ceremony will be streamed for free via UEFA.tv and the official UEFA YouTube channel.

Recent findings suggest that if Scotland fail to beat Switzerland in their final Group B1 game, they will be guaranteed to finish in the third place and will remain in League B for the next edition of the tournament. North Macedonia are already guaranteed to finish fourth place will face a promotion/relegation playoff game with a second-placed League C team to remain in League B. Scotland are safe from relegation to League B.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Switzerland have already won the group and have been promoted to League A. As detailed above, the second place team [currently Slovenia] will face a playoff against a third placed League A side.

Recent findings suggest that A third placed finish will have a direct effect on Scotland’s Euro 2028 qualifying campaign, which begins in March 2027. The tournament, which takes place across the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland, will require all four co-hosts - England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland - to compete in the standard qualifying campaign. They are not given a bye.

Sources indicate that where teams finish in their Nations League groups will directly decide how they are seeded for Euro 2028 qualifying, with each nation seeded based on their final group position. If Scotland finish in third, then Pocognoli’s side would drop into pot three for the draw, which could result in them facing high-ranking opponents from Pot 1 and Pot 2.

Sources indicate that the Euro 2028 qualifying draw sees teams separated into 12 groups of either four or five teams. Those who win their groups groups qualify automatically for the finals, alongside the eight highest ranked second place finishers. The four lowest ranked second place finishers enter the play-offs. Team who finish third or lower will not qualify.

The one caveat is that the host nations have two spots in the finals reserved if they fail to qualify. If more than two host teams do not qualify via the usual route, these two places will be allocated to the hosts placed highest in the European Qualifiers overall rankings. If only one or neither of the spots be used, the remaining places will be reallocated via the play-offs.

The absences have coincided with a run of just one win in eight matches across all competitions, leaving Wouter Vrancken's side fourth in the Scottish Premiership and 32nd in the Uefa Conference League.

"I need to look beyond the bad luck theory and dig into possible circumstances or reasons as to why we find ourselves where we are," Jones stated in a club interview. "We've got a new head coach that's brought in an intended new front foot style philosophy of how we play. We have new players who are adapting to a more competitive league than what they've been used to previously.

According to recent reports, "We have European football which is becoming the standard we want every season but the demands that Thursday-Sunday brings on the team. And then there's also the part of the bad luck which is we've suffered a huge amount of contact injuries so far this season, more in this short period than the whole of last season.

"So, unfortunate as it is, it's a convergence of all these factors. But I also think it's key to realise that there is light at the end of the tunnel. We have players returning for the game coming up on Saturday [away to Dundee].

Sources indicate that "We're hoping to have up to six, maybe even seven players possibly back into contention for first team training. Whether they're included in the squad, it just might be too soon, but we'll manage that accordingly. I can be confident that things are going to improve in the second half of the season, I've got no doubts on that.".

Jones reassured fans that Hearts are "not sitting on our hands" with regards to addressing their injury problems.

Sources indicate that he added: "We conducted an external review of our performance area at the turn of this year. We utilised one of the top performance practitioners in the the UK and he conducted an in-depth review that came with a numerous recommendations of things that we needed to improve. We've implemented all of these things.

"We have invested heavily in our medical department and even though it might not feel like it from the outside looking in, we're in a much better place to deal with this unprecedented level of injuries than we would have been a year ago.".

Sources indicate that hearts came into the campaign looking to build on last season's runners-up finish in the Scottish Premiership after narrowly missing out on a first title in 66 years to Celtic on the final day. However, after 12 matches, they have collected 10 points less than they had at the same stage last season with 12 more goals conceded. They also lost their 18-month unbeaten home record against Falkirk and were beaten by rivals Hibs at Hampden for the first time in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup.

"It's not been good enough," Jones admitted. "I know that, Wouter knows that, the players know that and we're doing everything during this international week to recalibrate and rest and put things right as best we can.

"It's vital to have the big picture in mind when you're in my role and looking towards the future. But I totally understand the short-term results have a massive effect on the general harmony across the board, particularly with our fans.

Recent findings suggest that "I would never sit here and tell fans to be patient and calm during these periods. I am a fan, I've sat in the stand during some of the worst times throughout the club's history so I do understand. But we as a club and me as the sporting director have to remain focused on the objectives and the long-term future of the club and the success of the club that we are striving for.".

Addressing Hearts' looks for the January transfer window, Jones, who was appointed sporting director two years ago, mentioned the focus would be on balancing the squad.

In a recent development, "We've got a very large squad with double figures number of players that are unavailable recently so as they return back we will naturally have to look at creating balance within the squad," he noted. "So we will look to decrease the size of the squad but also only add with quality. So it will be an active window like all transfer windows are but as we all know January is notoriously difficult.

Sources indicate that "We've got plenty of evidence in the last two years that the players that sign in January don't always come in and hit the ground running. So we have to focus our attentions on the quality that can make a difference but we will be very much looking to create a bit of balance within the squad. Once all our players come back are fit and available and then looking to add quality and also help people move on that aren't getting the opportunities.".

Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46.

#14414. Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in August 1987, a scandal erupted over work on the world’s highest mountain range.
  • More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.
  • More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a upcoming record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Illustration by Piotr Kowalczyk.

Industry observers note that in August 1987, a scandal erupted over work on the world’s highest mountain range. John Talent, a palaeontologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, revealed he had found numerous anomalies in research charting the geology of the Himalayas. All of the problems were in papers by Vishwa Jit Gupta, one of India’s most celebrated palaeontologists at the time.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a upcoming record.

Gupta was outraged. But further investigations over the following seven years revealed the scale and brazenness of his fraud. Littered through more than 450 publications were maps of collection sites that didn’t exist, plagiarized images and specimens stolen from collections that Gupta had visited. More than 100 experts had been duped into co-authoring descriptions of fossils Gupta claimed he had collected from specific Himalayan geological formations, but instead hailed from North America and Morocco.

“It destroyed the image of Indian science,” notes retired geologist Ghulam Bhat, who completed his PhD on Himalayan geology in the same year that the allegations of fraud emerged.

Gupta died in 2022, and many geologists know to steer clear of his work. But awareness of the problem is fading, and none of Gupta’s papers have been retracted. When Nature contacted Bhat, who is now editor-in-chief of the Journal of the Geological Society of India (JGSI), he was unaware that Gupta’s papers were not marked as retracted. That’s despite the JGSI’s 1991 evaluation of 19 of Gupta’s papers that it published1, which concluded that “the fossil finds of V. J. Gupta are not reliable [...] the data is incomplete bordering on disinformation”.

According to recent reports, much of Gupta’s work is inaccessible, having been published in now-defunct periodicals or in volumes that, although digitized online, have not been indexed in reference bibliometric databases such as Scopus, Web of Science and Dimensions. Despite this, Gupta’s falsehoods are now being propagated outside specialist circles, as his old journal articles are being surfaced through artificial-intelligence tools that summarize search results. When someone searches for geological landmarks in the Himalayas, such as the Tandi Limestone, Google’s AI overview obliges with direct links to Gupta’s discredited papers.

Bhat now prepares to rectify the digital record and says that all other journals that have published Gupta’s work should do the same. “If this problem is left as it is, unattended, it will pollute all of the geological literature in future,” he says. Gupta also published papers in Nature in the 1960s; Chris Graf, director of research integrity at Springer Nature, didn’t confirm that the journal would re-examine them. But he added that in general, when investigations of old papers are hampered by limited available information, an editorial expression of concern “is likely to be our preferred mechanism for alerting readers to potential complications”. (Nature’s news team is editorially independent of its publisher, Springer Nature.).

The Himalayas case raises a wider issue: how to deal with fraudulent, unethical or even merely incorrect research from decades ago, especially in an era in which much old work is digitized and AI systems can pick up studies that might previously have been neglected.

There are many skeletons in science’s closet, but publishers can be reluctant to judge science of the past by today’s standards, and can find it more difficult to glitch retractions when authors are dead, original records cannot be consulted or journals are no longer in print.

And as publishers struggle to deal with the fallout from rising research fraud and AI slop, finite resources can also mean that many old papers with known flaws are left as they are.

Gráinne McNamara, a council member of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in Eastleigh, UK, which advises journals on best practice, says that journals are increasingly contacting COPE to ask for advice about dealing with concerns on very old papers.

“Everybody is looking for what’s the best, most responsible way to handle these,” she claims.

It has been revealed that the widespread use of retractions as a mechanism for maintaining integrity in the scientific record is a relatively recent phenomenon. The JGSI evaluation report about Gupta served as a warning notice to the community at the time, but didn’t use the word retraction. It also pre-dates the modern standardization of retraction processes, which happened in the 2000s. Now, a journal should issue a retraction notice, and leave the original paper intact, but with a modified title and a stamp or watermark indicating that it has been retracted. The information should then feed through to bibliographic databases.

According to recent reports, in the early 2000s, only around 30 retraction notices were published each year, and COPE first developed guidelines to standardize the retraction process in 2004. The number — and rate — of retractions has exploded since then, with more than 10,000 recorded in 2023 alone.

Recent findings suggest that digitization of old records, combined with a wider propensity to retract flawed work, has seen journals reaching farther back in time to retract studies — and this has led to some startlingly long gaps between when an article was published and when it was formally retracted. Retraction Watch, an initiative that curates a database of more than 70,000 retractions and expressions of concern (a notice that highlights potential challenges with a publication), has reported that the longest gap is 80 years. That’s for a prank case report published in 1923 in the Dutch medical journal Nederlands Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde.

It described a man who died from “piss cough”, an affliction that caused him to cough up liquid smelling of urine. In 2003, an editor at the journal happened to look up the case, which he thought was widely known to be a hoax. Realizing it had never been retracted and that others did not know it was fake, he sought confirmation of the hoax, and found it in the autobiography of a retired University of Amsterdam physician, who had helped to cook up the nonsense case when he was a medical student. Accompanying commentary on the journal’s website mentioned that a retraction was appropriate now that the older literature had become accessible through digitization.

According to recent reports, according to Nature’s analysis of Retraction Watch data — which capture a subset of total retractions — the number of old papers that are being retracted is rising. Overall, some 358 retraction notices and 120 expressions of concern have been issued for papers or book chapters that were more than 20 years old at the time of the editorial action (see ‘Retracting the past’). This is still a rare phenomenon: since 2015, the oldest retractions represent some 0.7% of the total number, up from 0.2% before 2010. But around 3% of expressions of concern have occurred for works older than 20 years. That illustrates how publishers might choose to concern expressions of concern for older papers, rather than retract, because it can be harder to investigate historical records.

In a recent development, in 2005, biochemist Barry Milborrow sought to retract five of his own papers, published between 1980 and 1982, on biochemical pathways that bacteria, algae and plants use to make pigments, because later work had disproved their findings. The Biochemical Journal, which published Milborrow’s self-retraction listing the five articles2, retracted both articles it had published. Another journal issued a correction, but no notice was issued by the publisher of the remaining two papers. Ian Swift, Milborrow’s co-author and PhD student at the University of Fresh South Wales in Sydney, Australia, at the time, says he only found out about the retractions many years later, after Milborrow had passed away.

According to recent reports, according to COPE guidance, journal editors can retract articles if they no longer have confidence in the results and conclusions reported in them. By that rubric, many older papers could, in theory, be retracted, but, being rarely cited, are usually left alone.

It has been revealed that even when invalid papers are still being cited, retraction might not follow. In 1985, for instance, geneticist Svante Pääbo reported that he had cloned DNA from an Egyptian mummy3. The seminal work marked the birth of palaeogenomics, a field that earned Pääbo a Nobel prize in 2022. But the mummy DNA was actually contamination from a modern handler, as Pääbo, now at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany, has openly acknowledged. “What is problematic is if false conclusions lead other scientists and the community as a whole astray,” he told Nature when asked for this article. “I don’t think anyone is currently misled by the mummy paper,” he says, which is why he argues that the work should stand, adding that to correct very old papers with errors “would create more confusion than clarity”.

Retractions can reshape scientists’ careers in unexpected ways.

Retractions can reshape scientists’ careers in unexpected ways.

In practice, old papers tend to be considered for retraction only if they have widespread integrity issues that journal editors feel shouldn’t be allowed to stand unmarked. A major trigger for mass retractions of older work is when investigations of an individual’s research cast doubt over their entire body of work. For instance, a 2019 investigation by King’s College London into the work of psychologist Hans Eysenck and his German collaborator Ronald Grossarth-Maticek has led to papers dating back to the 1940s being flagged — albeit many with expressions of concern rather than retractions.

Recent findings suggest that eysenck died in 1997 as one of the most celebrated psychologists of the twentieth century. But in 2019, psychiatrist Anthony Pelosi, who had critiqued Eysenck’s work to no effect in the 1990s, published a renewed analysis of the studies4. An accompanying editorial called on King’s College London — where Eysenck worked from 1955 until 1983 — to conduct a formal investigation. The investigation report, also published in 2019, concluded that 24 articles by Eysenck and Maticek published between 1988 and 2000 were ‘unsafe’ and recommended they be retracted.

Those recommendations weren’t followed entirely. Only 16 of the 24 papers have been retracted, and another 4 have expressions of concern. Four remain unflagged. After sustained criticism over the narrow scope of the 2019 investigation, King’s College London published a statement in October 2025 saying that other publications based on the data set used in the 24 papers it examined are also likely to be ‘unsafe’ and should be flagged by journal editors — although it did not list affected publications.

So far, 94 of Eysenck’s hundreds of papers have been either retracted or tagged with an expression of concern, the oldest of which was published in 1943 (see ‘Longest gaps’).

Such inconsistencies in how publishers deal with research-integrity complications are common and don’t relate only to very old papers, says Andrew Grey, an endocrinologist and research-integrity specialist at the University of Auckland in New Zealand. He alerted publishers to concerns over large numbers of articles by Yoshihiro Sato, a Japanese bone-health researcher who fabricated data in dozens of clinical trials, and has reported seeing some journals respond with retractions or expressions of concern, whereas others take no action5.

One famous scandal of the past — the 1980s discrediting of work by John Darsee, a US biologist — has led to just 17 retractions. Although news reports at the time stated that more than 80 of Darsee’s papers had been retracted, this refers to editorial notes and warnings that, in parallel with the Gupta case, don’t appear in modern records as retractions.

Another trigger for retracting old work is when it attracts renewed attention, particularly in medical fields.

Each year, Marcel van der Heyden, a physiologist at the University Medical Center Utrecht in the Netherlands, asks his final-year students to write a review article about a poison or toxin. In 2025, he chose caesium salts, and his students uncovered 20 case reports of people ingesting the toxic chemical6. Often, the individuals deliberately consumed the compound as an alternative treatment for cancer. Although the US Food and Drug Administration cautioned against its use in 2018, the deadly ‘therapy’ is still promoted in books and online by some wellness centres.

According to recent reports, the treatment traces back to two papers published in 1984 in Pharmacology Biochemistry and Behavior. One of the papers was written by Austrian-born Hellfried Sartori, who had been prosecuted in Maryland in 1982 for fraud relating to using the unproven cancer treatment. That case ended in a mistrial. Sartori subsequently had his medical licence revoked in several US states in the 1980s and was sentenced to prison in Virginia in 1999 for practising medicine without a licence. And in 2010, an inquest into the deaths of five people in Australia found that he had been treating patients remotely from Thailand. Many more of his patients had also died under his treatment, the court heard.

The other paper promoting caesium therapy was by Wisconsin-based Aubrey Keith Brewer. Brewer died in 1986, but his namesake Brewer International Science Library continues to distribute information on caesium and other alternative therapies with a disclaimer that the protocols are “for information purposes only”, and that people should consult their physician if unwell. Nature contacted the website but received no response.

Van der Heyden contacted Pharmacology Biochemistry and Behavior in August 2025, suggesting an expression of concern could be warranted. “Without the original data, it’s hard to tell whether there is a mistake made, or whether it’s on purpose,” he says. But the research-integrity team at the journal’s publisher, Elsevier, decided in January this year to remove the two papers, soon after Van der Heyden informed them that his review had been accepted for publication and that his university was poised to issue a press release about it. The papers were deleted entirely this April, as Retraction Watch reported.

The move to scrub a paper, rather than merely retract and leave it in place, can be taken if the contents could present a serious health risk to the public, according to COPE guidelines.
