📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 21:57, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 22:05.

Africa Cup of Nations co-hosts Tanzania will be seeking their first win of the qualifiers when they welcome Nigeria to the Amaan Stadium on Tuesday.

While the match carries little significance for the hosts - already assured of a place at next year’s finals - the visitors remain fully focused, as a win would all but secure their own qualification.

It has been revealed that no team in AFCON history has recorded more podium finishes (17) than Nigeria, who are regulars at the competition. After wins over Madagascar and Tanzania, either side of a 3-0 defeat to Guinea Bissau, the West Africans are on course to reach the tournament finals once again.

Despite missing several key attacking players, Eric Chelle’s men scored three goals in a competitive match for the first time since January, hinting at attacking depth across the squad, which is crucial given their overreliance on Victor Osimhen at times.

The Super Eagles have topped their AFCON qualifying group in each of the last four campaigns but currently trail Guinea Bissau by three points, so they cannot afford further slip-ups if they hope to finish as group winners.

Winless in their last four outings (D2, L2), Tuesday's visitors have been underwhelming away from home lately, so supporters travelling to Zanzibar City will be wary of further disappointment, with September’s heavy defeat in Bissau still fresh in the memory.

Converting just 10% of their chances so far, Nigeria need a much sharper edge in front of goal, especially given their ongoing defensive woes, having now gone six matches without a clean sheet since a 3-0 win over Jamaica in May.

While the result was inconsequential in the grand scheme, Tanzania were largely competitive in the first half of their 3-1 defeat to Nigeria, but a lacklustre second-half display set the stage for a second defeat in three outings.

Miguel Angel Gamondi’s men would have hoped the AFCON qualifiers might provide a preview of what to expect on their fifth appearance at the competition next year. However, based on recent results, hopes of a fairytale showing on home soil are quickly diminishing.

The Taifa Stars have now won just one of their last 16 matches across all competitions - a run that includes two meetings with Nigeria, who are unbeaten in seven previous encounters, winning five.

Tanzania are still awaiting their first competitive home victory since being awarded a 3-0 win over Congo in March 2025. As a result, some sections of the nation's faithful will approach this clash hoping for the best but expecting the worst.

A good start would help settle any nerves, but Tuesday’s hosts have conceded first in five of their last seven outings, and a repeat of that would be catastrophic, to say the least, given their current dry patch.

Tanzania form (all competitions):.

Nigeria Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Nigeria form (all competitions):.

Ademola Lookman and Victor Osimhen are both ruled out with knee injuries, after Lookman was forced off just before half-time on Friday.

Igoh Ogbu (Achilles) and Samuel Chukwueze (thigh) are also unavailable for the visitors, who continue to monitor the fitness of Frank Onyeka.

Tolu Arokodare came off the bench to score twice last time out and could be rewarded with a start here as he looks to continue his impressive run of form.

Ibrahim Hamad is Tanzania’s most notable absentee due to a knock, following an impressive display at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium.

This should open the door for Charles M’Mombwa to come into the hosts’ starting XI, although Evastus Lukanima could also be considered.

Tanzania possible starting lineup:.

Manula; Mligo, M’Mombwa, Mwamnyeto, Mnoga; Miroshi, Mkami, Msanga, Chilambo; Kachwele, Kibu.

Nigeria possible starting lineup:.

Nwabali; Aina, Bassey, Fredrick, Bewene; Yusuf, Iwobi, Ndidi, Nnadi; Arokodare, Adams.

Despite the Super Eagles being far from full strength, anything less than a win here would be considered an underperformance.

With two leaky defences on display, goals are likely at both ends, but we expect the away side to come out on top when all is said and done.

A Scotland side still finding their feet under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli conclude their Nations League B1 campaign on Monday night when they face group winners Switzerland in St Gallen.

Pocognoli earned the first home win of his tenure at the third attempt on Friday with a 2-1 win over North Macedonia but the unconvicing performance suggested the Belgian still has work to do to get the best out of his squad.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Switzerland have already secured automatic promotion to Nations League A after collecting 13 points from their five matches thus far, including a 3-0 win over 10-man Scotland at Hampden on September 29.

But while the hosts can relax, the game is not a dead rubber for Scotland, who can still claim a runners-up finish in the section with what would be a famous away victory over the side ranked 12th in the Fifa world rankings - 31 places above them.

The game is also hugely significant for captain Andy Robertson who will become Scotland’s most capped player, eclipsing Kenny Dalglish by reaching 103 appearances, if he plays on the night as expected.

It has been revealed that scotland will only finish second in Group B1 if they beat the Swiss and Slovenia fail to collect three points against North Macedonia in Skopje. Slovenia, on eight points, are one point ahead of Scotland in the standings but have a superior head-to-head record after their 2-1 win at Hampden last month that will see them claim the higher spot in the table if the sides finish on the same number of points.

According to recent reports, second place for Scotland would secure a Nations League promotion play-off in March against one of the third-placed teams from a Group A section. It would also guarantee pot two seeding for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place next month. If Scotland finish third in Nations League B1, they will drop into pot three and face high-ranking teams in pots one and two.

It has been revealed that the Nations League B1 fixture between Switzerland and Scotland takes place at Berit Sitterstadion in St. Gallen on Monday, November 16, 2026. Kick-off is 7.45pm.

The match will be broadcast live on BBC 2 and the BBC Scotland channel with coverage starting at 7.30pm.

The game can be live streamed for free on the BBC Sport website and the BBC iPlayer.

Industry observers note that scotland picked up no fresh injury concerns against North Macedonia on Friday but head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is expected to make changes. “I will need to consider the best approach for the game regarding the quality and also the fitness of some players,” he stated. “We have some players in the squad who we have to manage. They cannot play two games in a row.”.

Industry observers note that switzerland, meanwhile, are expected to rotate their squad. Head coach Murat Yakin will be without Internazionale defender Manuel Akanji, captain Granit Xhaka of Sunderland, Aston Villa's Johan Manzambi and Nottingham Forest winger Dan Ndoye. Yakin revealed that 20-year-old Sion striker Winsley Boteli will earn his fourth senior cap, while 23-year-old Young Boys midfielder Alvyn Sanches will be handed his seventh, both from the start.

In a recent development, the entire officiating team is from the Netherlands with referee Danny Makkelie taking charge on the field. He is joined by assistant referees Hessel Steegstra and Jan de Vries, with Alex Bos acting as the fourth official. Erwin Blank serves as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), who will be joined in the VAR booth by Jeroen Manschot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

In a recent development, it felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Sources indicate that their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

Sources indicate that in the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k.

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

Recent findings suggest that this is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

It has been revealed that instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

In a recent development, they are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

Recent findings suggest that in the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other significant signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

Erling Haaland gives Manchester City the lead against Liverpool 🎯 https://t.co/cELo5y60Fk.

Industry observers note that in fact, Liverpool’s best performers were the young attackers Victor Muñoz and, making his first league start as a makeshift centre-forward, Lewis Koumas, who is just 21. Against that, City unleashed a battery of forward talent.

Was it an unfair advantage? It appears City have been thriving off that for some time and, while this team were not signed during the years the club have been found guilty of cheating, the argument is, of course, that they would not have joined without the sporting supremacy.

Certainly not Haaland, despite his avowed love for City. That cannot be doubted as his father, Alf-Inge, a former midfielder for the club, stood celebrating in the away end. The striker missed one chance when he should have scored, sent through on goal, shaking his head in disbelief at getting his angles wrong. It felt like a warning and that went unheeded as Doku, who had replaced one of their big summer signings in Iliman Ndiaye, cut in from the left with his shot deflecting into Haaland’s path. He made no mistake with a powerful, first-time finish.

Doku soon added a second, a sublime strike, as he dribbled goalwards, defenders backing off, and he arced a right-footed shot high beyond Alisson Becker’s grasp.

"It's a GEM" 💎 A beautiful strike from Jérémy Doku to double Man City's lead! https://t.co/lCUFfQmdLC.

There were delighted chants of “olé” from the City supporters and that arrogance was rewarded by a strutting, emphatic third goal. It was finished by the mercurial Rayan Cherki after he was sent clear by a backheel from Josko Gvardiol, another substitute.

A moment of individual brilliance from Rayan Cherki to put the game beyond all doubt 🤯 https://t.co/wvmTMZcGhW.

Sources indicate that it captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. In a sea of uncertainty as to what will now happen, that is something we can be sure of.

“Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Those signs of defiance were not matched on the pitch. Although it may be a song City will get used to hearing for the rest of this extraordinary, unprecedented campaign.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

Industry observers note that “It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, mentioned. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”.

Maresca said City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”.

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”.

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

In a recent development, “The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he stated. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”.

The Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

According to recent reports, “The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”.

Scotland’s Nations League campaign wraps up on Monday evening with a tough encounter against Switzerland as the side aims to snatch an unlikely promotion playoff spot in Group B1 from Slovenia.

Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli finally got his first home win with a 2-1 win over North Macedonia on Friday, and now his team will look to make it back-to-back wins for the first time under his management while hoping Slovenia slip up in the group’s other game.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It has been revealed that however, should Scotland fail to win in St Gallen, hopes of promotion back to League A will be extinguished. A third-place finish will also have ramifications for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifiers, which are drawn in Belfast this December.

It has been revealed that but when did Scotland last beat Switzerland? What is their head-to-head record, and when did they last meet? Here’s everything you need to know about Scotland’s record against Switzerland.

The teams have faced each other a total of 18 times, and have met twice in major tournament finals, with both encounters taking place in the group stage of the European Championships.

They last faced each other just last month in the Nations League, where Switzerland ran out 3-0 winners after Jack Hendry was sent off early on at Hampden Park. Prior to that game, they drew 1-1 at Euro 2024 in Germany, with Scott McTominay opening the scoring early on for Scotland, before Xherdan Shaqiri equalised shortly afterwards.

From their 18 games played, Scotland have eight wins, giving them a 33.3% win percentage. Switzerland have won a total of six times - a 22.22 per cent win percentage. A further four games have ended in a draw.

Industry observers note that despite having the better head to head record against the Swiss, the Scotland men’s national team have not tasted victory against them for over 30 years. Their most recent win came at Euro 1996 at Villa Park, Birmingham on 18 June, where they earned their first win a 1-0 win in their final group game at the tournament.

According to recent reports, the victory came via a fine strike from Ally McCoist in the 36th minute, but was not enough for Scotland to qualify for the knockout stages of the tournament, with the Netherlands finishing above them on goal difference. The Switzerland side that day included future Celtic defender Ramon Vega.

Scotland line up that night: Andy Goram, Tom Boyd, Colin Calderwood, Colin Hendry, Stuart McCall, Gary McAllister, John Collins, Tosh McKinlay (Scott Booth, 60), Craig Burley, Gordon Durie and Ally McCoist (John Spencer, 84).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 23:18.

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is obsessed with the idea of signing Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk, the latest report has revealed.

The Reds' centre-back has so far enjoyed a strong season in England, helping the Merseysiders keep four clean sheets in their first 10 Premier League games.

However, fans are worried about the Dutchman's future given his contract is set to expire at the end of the campaign.

The 35-year-old has hinted that he would like to stay at Anfield, but there has seemingly been little movement regarding an extension.

Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport now claim that AC Milan's majority shareholder Cardinale is obsessed with the idea of signing Van Dijk.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) have implemented a policy focused on rewarding younger stars at the club, while also moving on experienced players before they decline beyond the point of use.

There have been exceptions to those rules, with Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah both signing deals in 2025 following impressive seasons.

However, Salah struggled considerably in 2025-26 before leaving for free in the summer transfer window, and it would be understandable if the club were reluctant about handing another deal to a player in the twilight of their career.

Van Dijk's performances may be deserving of a contract offer, but FSG are unlikely to be swayed by any sentiment shared by fans, and they will instead make an emotionless judgement call in 2027.

Van Dijk is still one of the most physically imposing defenders in Europe, with the centre-back having won 75% of his duels in the Premier League this season.

Losing his experience would place significant pressure on Jeremy Jacquet next term, and the 21-year-old would benefit from spending more time without being the main man at the back for Andoni Iraola.

Liverpool are also likely to lose Alisson Becker and Joe Gomez for free in the summer, so ensuring there is someone at the club that has been through the peaks and troughs of life at Anfield would be sensible.

Scotland year that started with promise ends in another setback amid fears over one player’s career

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A year that started so full of promise for Scotland ground to a humiliating halt in St Gallen. The 13th match of a World Cup dominated 12 months always threatened to be the toughest of tough tasks.

Recent findings suggest that not perhaps as challenging as taking on Brazil in Miami or Morocco in Boston. But Switzerland, World Cup quarter-finalists themselves, are no pushovers, as they proved in a match of supposedly little consequence for them. Having already secured top place in Group B1, they enjoyed the luxury of making changes and still eased to a deserved 4-0 victory in the university city.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Industry observers note that what did Sebastien Pocognoli learn? Not too much as he watched his side picked apart by Murat Yakin’s exciting team. Two goals just after the break – a tap in from Winsley Boteli and a rocket from Alvyn Sanches – rendered the second half little more than a training exercise.

In a recent development, substitute Zeki Amdouni wrapped things up in the final minute with a shot from the edge of the of the box that took a wicked deflection off Luke Graham. It was that kind of night. Lewis Ferguson had put through his own goal to set the Swiss on their way after 22 minutes.

Sources indicate that it was anything but the much-needed statement result for Pocognoli some had surmised might be possible against hosts who could afford to coast. Instead, there were fears that Switzerland – 3-0 up after just 51 minutes – would pile on the pain.

Scotland suffered a 7-0 defeat against Uruguay 80 or so miles away in Basel at the 1954 World Cup and something as embarrassing felt possible, particularly when the "oles" from the home fans were ringing around the Sitterstadion early in the second half.

It has been revealed that this wasn’t how Andy Robertson, who had 103 stitched into the tongues of his boots, wanted to become Scotland’s most-capped ever men’s player. Scotland were completely licked.

Sanches missed an open goal with eight minutes left after Angus Gunn miscued a pass, although the Swiss forward was around 50 yards out. The keeper did well to block a later shot from the same player but was helpless when Amdouni’s deflected effort looped into the net for 4-0.

Of course, it helps when the opposition scores the all-key first goal for you. Ferguson inadvertently put through his own net as he attempted to cut out the danger following Zachary Athekame’s cross from the right. Not too long afterwards, about 900 miles away in Skopje, Slovenia scored their opener against North Macedonia to further put the Scots behind the black ball in their quest to finish in second place. The Slovenians ended up winning 3-0, leaving Scotland in a very distant third place in the group and wondering what the future holds. At least there are no more games until March. It’s been a tough old year. The memorable moments have almost all occurred off the pitch. It isn’t all on Pocognoli, granted.

Recent findings suggest that what was underlined here is that the Belgian could do with a bit of fortune. He could do with the stars aligning in the way they did for Steve Clarke a year ago this week, when everything seemed to fall into place eventually on a night of nights against Denmark in Glasgow.

In a recent development, pocognoli, by contrast, is struggling to get going. His Hampden bow against Switzerland was ruined by Jack Hendry’s red card just ten minutes in. Here he saw Scott McTominay blaze over from six yards and watched John McGinn place a header straight into the hands of keeper Yvon Mvogo.

Recent findings suggest that more serious woe arrived in the form of the latest injury misery to befall Aaron Hickey. The former Hearts player’s left hamstring has proved troublesome for a few managers, including Clarke, and obviously for the player himself.

According to recent reports, it was heartbreaking to see the player stumble having performed a typically diligent defensive duty, in this case mopping up by directing a header into Gunn’s arms. He also pulled something in the process and made a sad exit down the tunnel after 36 minutes, with Nathan Patterson replacing him. Brentford will be furious although it’s not as if Pocognoli hadn’t sought to manage the player’s minutes.

Sources indicate that he left him out of the first game of the window against North Macedonia. This latest setback feels bigger than just what it means for Pocognoli and Scotland. It raises real fears about a brilliant young player’s career.

So the outcome of the match, as dispiriting as the defeat was, needs to be placed in context. It might have proved a happier evening had Hickey’s header from Andy Robertson’s cross 24 minutes sneaked in rather than past the post just minutes after Ferguson’s own goal horror.

In a recent development, hickey was also in the thick of things after a clever touch from Oli McBurnie saw him burst into the Swiss half. Kieran Tierney was to his left and was screaming to be played in but the wing-back just could not get the ball out of his feet and the chance was gone.

Ferguson’s misery was all the more frustrating because it was so unnecessary. Ryan Porteous was waiting to clear but the Bologna midfielder got in before him and steered past Gunn while attempting to clear the danger.

The game was over six minutes into the second half. Ballet exchanged passes with Remo Feuler and shot towards goal. Although Boteli probably didn’t need to help the ball over the line, he did anyway at the risk of seeing the goal chalked off for offside.

According to recent reports, he was just onside and was credited with the strike. There was no doubt who scored the third for the hosts, with Sanches latching on to a loose ball after Patterson had been dispossessed before rifling into the corner past Gunn.

Sources indicate that the loss of a fourth goal seemed inconsequential but did seem to sum everything up. These are very different times to 12 months ago and more hurt may lie ahead.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 23:27.

Nicaragua and Montserrat will face off in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League play-in tie at the Nicaragua National Football Stadium in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time.

The Blue and White claimed a 2-1 victory away from home in the first leg and will head into the return fixture full of confidence as they look to finish the job in front of their home supporters.

Juan Cruz Real's side have endured a horror Nations League campaign, failing to pick up a single point from four matches.

They have scored only four goals and conceded 14 as they finished at the bottom of League A's Group A.

After four defeats in a row, Nicaragua produced a strong performance at Estadio Cibao, where they took full advantage of an extra man after the home side were reduced to 10 men inside the opening 20 minutes.

Despite going a goal down, an own goal from Samuel Fenton sparked a revival, while Efrain Mejia scored in the 72nd minute to give them a slender lead heading into the second leg.

Montserrat are the underdogs in this tie, having earned their place in the play-in round from League C, but they have shown few weaknesses so far.

Despite losing a man so early in the first leg, they still managed to find the net, meaning the tie remains very much in the balance heading into the return fixture.

Gabriel Calderon's side won all four of their matches in League C's Group A, scoring 11 goals and conceding just once.

Montserrat kept clean sheets in three of those outings, but they have never tasted victory against their opponents in four attempts, which could prove a psychological hurdle.

Nicaragua could look to field a similar side to the one that started the first leg, although Cruz Real may be tempted to hand right-winger Mejia a starting role after his impressive performance earlier this week.

Juan Barrera failed to make a significant impact in the previous match, but he is still likely to retain his place, with Jaime Moreno once again expected to make a cameo appearance from the bench.

The visitors will definitely be without Lenni Cirino, who was sent off in the first leg.

Captain Alex Dyer appeared to pick up an injury towards the closing stages of that encounter before being replaced by Vashim Roache, and his absence would represent a major blow.

Tyrone Baker may have to settle for a place on the bench, but versatile midfielder Kaleem Simon could come into the starting XI.

Nicaragua possible starting lineup:.

Mayorga; Gutierrez, Cano, Perez, Quijano; R Cole, Salinas, Hernandez, Mejia, Talavera; Smith.

Montserrat possible starting lineup:.

Carter-Rodgers; Cirino, Furlong, Dorsett, Townsend-West; Barzey, Kirnon, Dyer, Simon; Comley, Boatswain.

Nicaragua have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last six matches and have conceded the opening goal in five of those encounters. However, buoyed by their first-leg victory, we expect the hosts to produce a stronger performance on home soil and narrowly secure another win.

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be big on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the new man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

According to recent reports, ‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Striker Adams says Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

According to recent reports, john McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

‘He stated to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very notable to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ noted Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.

  • Sierra Leone and Congo DR return to action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they square off in the second of their Group E double-header at the Stade El Abdi on Tuesday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Ojele | 15 Nov 2026 23:31, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 23:32.

Sierra Leone and Congo DR return to action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they square off in the second of their Group E double-header at the Stade El Abdi on Tuesday.

While the Leopards will look to maintain their 100% record in the qualifiers and move another step closer to securing their place in next year’s continental showpiece, Sierra Leone head into the game under considerable pressure for a result, having lost their three matches so far.

Tasked with guiding Sierra Leone to a first Africa Cup of Nations tournament since 2022, French head coach Didier Gomes Da Rosa has failed to make his mark in the qualifiers, with the Lone Stars rooted to the bottom of Group E after the first half of the campaign.

While they revealed signs of promise, Sierra Leone blew a two-goal lead in the group opener on September 24, when they fell to a 3-2 loss against Zimbabwe in Morocco, four days before suffering a 1-0 loss at the hands of Equatorial Guinea at the Stade Omnisport Ahmadou Ahidjo.

Sierra Leone were left with a mountain to climb in the qualifiers on Thursday, when they were beaten 3-1 by DR Congo, with Yoane Wissa, Samuel Moutoussamy and Watford man Edo Kayembe hitting the back of the net to fire the Leopards to all three points.

Having missed out on the 2025 AFCON after an underwhelming qualifying campaign that saw them finish third in Group G with five points from six matches, Sierra Leone are one of just six sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, leaving them with little margin for further errors and in need of significant improvement.

Meanwhile, Congo DR kicked off their AFCON qualifying journey on a high, claiming a 2-0 victory over Equatorial Guinea on September 24, four days before edging out Zimbabwe 2-1 at the National Sports Stadium thanks to strikes from Wissa and Moutoussamy.

However, a break from competitive action saw the Leopards fail to win their subsequent two outings, losing 2-0 against Uganda on October 2, three days before playing out a 1-1 stalemate with the Cranes in the second of their friendly double-header at the FNB Stadium.

Congo DR returned to action in the AFCON qualifiers with a comprehensive team display against Sierra Leone on Thursday to remain one of just four nations with a 100% record in the campaign and move one step closer to sealing a third appearance in the continental tournament since missing out in 2021.

Sebastien Desabre’s men, who are currently 40th in the latest FIFA World Rankings, sit top of the Group E standings with nine points from a possible nine, five points above Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea, who sit level on four points after the first three games.

Congo DR will be backing themselves to maintain their perfect record on Tuesday when they take on an opposing side who have lost each of their previous four meetings, conceding 11 goals and scoring just twice since September 2014.

Sierra Leone Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Sierra Leone form (all competitions):.

Congo DR Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Congo DR form (all competitions):.

Sierra Leone came out unscathed against DR Congo on Thursday, and we expect Da Rosa to name a similar XI at the Stade El Abdi, with Alie Conteh and Elfsborg striker Momoh Kamara spearheading the attack.

Amidst their struggles at the defensive end of the pitch, Da Rosa could opt for a change in the back four, with Alpha Turay, who made his debut in June 2023, coming into the mix to form the centre-back pairing with Kilmarnock man Michael John Kamara.

As for DR Congo, APS Atromitos Athinon midfielder Moutoussamy was forced off injured midway through Thursday’s clash, and the 30-year-old is a doubt for Tuesday’s matchup.

Should he fail to shake off the injury, Lorient man Noah Mbamba, who made his debut on Thursday, will push for his first start in the Leopards’ colours, teaming up with Edo Kayembe and Sunderland man Noah Sadiki at the centre of the park.

Up top, Wissa made it three goals in three AFCON qualifying games with his opener against Sierra Leone on Thursday, and the Newcastle United striker should lead the attack once again, forming the front three with Nathanael Mbuku and Almeria winger Brian Cipenga.

Sierra Leone possible starting lineup:.

Sesay; Kakay, MJ Kamara, J. Turay, Tarawallie; Kanu, I.Turay, Kamara, Koroma; M. Kamara, Conteh.

Congo DR possible starting lineup:.

Epolo; Pedro, Mbemba, Tuanzebe, Masuaku; Kayembe, Mbamba, Sadiki; Mbuku, Wissa, Cipenga.

With three games played already, Tuesday’s result will prove decisive in determining Sierra Leone’s qualifying fate, and we expect the Lone Stars to go all out at the Stade El Abdi as they look to get their campaign back on track.

Congo DR, who have shown their class in Group E so far, boast the quality and experience across the pitch to get the result here, and we are backing them to continue from where they left off on Thursday, extending their hot streak against Sierra Leone.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A second-half collapse against a second-string Swiss side who had already secured promotion to League A condemned the Scots to their heaviest loss since their 5-1 thrashing by Germany at Euro 2024.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sebastien Pocognoli has insisted Scotland’s bruising 4-0 defeat to Switzerland was not a fair reflection of the contest as their Nations League campaign ended on a sour note in St Gallen.

A second-half collapse against a second-string Swiss side who had already secured promotion to League A condemned the Scots to their heaviest loss since their 5-1 thrashing by Germany at Euro 2024.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The result leaves Pocognoli's men third in Group B1 with seven points from six matches. It also means Scotland will enter the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in Belfast in a couple of weeks in pot three, potentially presenting a more challenging route towards the tournament.

However, the head coach was keen to highlight the positives from his side's performance, particularly their first-half display, arguing that the final scoreline was harsh on his players.

Recent findings suggest that “The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game, if I'm really honest and objective," Pocognoli noted. “We had some very good moments in the game, we started the game like we wanted, aggressive away from home. We could decide to be low on the pitch, but we did what we wanted to plan.”.

Lewis Ferguson's unfortunate own goal handed Switzerland the advantage, but the visitors responded well and created opportunities through Andy Robertson, Aaron Hickey and John McGinn.

Pocognoli felt his side had done enough to trouble the hosts before the interval, despite failing to convert their promising openings.

"We played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments in the game, and we faced Switzerland with different shapes and adapted well from the first minute,” he continued. “We conceded the goal from maybe one of the first chances they had. We also created chances, but we missed it. It means we were not clinical in that moment in the box.”.

Recent findings suggest that the second half, however, exposed Scotland's defensive vulnerabilities in alarming fashion. The Swiss scored twice within six minutes of the restart through Winsley Boteli and Alvyn Sanches, effectively ending the contest.

Pocognoli admitted his team’s start to the second period was unacceptable, adding: “We started poorly from the first minute, a poor corner we gave away. Then you feel that, OK, we will get punished. But I think when we made the substitutions, they made an impact, and we should have scored two goals in that period.

“We got punished for the same reason like in the first half. At the end, it's a bad feeling, the score, but I think that the players try to do their best and create moments that we want to see.”.

Despite the emphatic nature of the defeat, the Belgian was adamant there were enough encouraging signs that his players were beginning to understand his more progressive style, even if the execution remains inconsistent.

According to recent reports, “If we were in confidence, we would not produce the moments we produce in the game," he summarised. “We create good moments on the ball, on pure bravery decisions to play forward through the lines or the pressure. We create chances also for pressing, sometimes we should have to manage better the transition from pressing, but it is all the things we want to see.

Sources indicate that “So the next step is to have the quality to just finish this action, and the more we have games together, the more we will try to fix these things. We have a lot of good response from this camp and it's good for the future as well.”.

Marks out of ten for how the Scotland players fared against Switzerland at Berit Sitterstadion in St. Gallen.

Scotland suffered a miserable 4-0 Nations League defeat against Switzerland in St Gallen as Andy Robertson’s record-breaking 103rd international appearance was overshadowed by a second-half collapse.

Sebastien Pocognoli’s side started brightly, pressing with greater intensity and creating some promising openings. However, their positive start was undone in the 22nd minute when Lewis Ferguson inadvertently turned Zachary Athekame’s cross into his own net.

The visitors responded well, with Aaron Hickey heading narrowly wide from Robertson’s excellent delivery, but the visitors were unable to find an equaliser before the break. Brentford right-back Hickey’s evening was also cut short by another hamstring injury, forcing him off after 36 minutes.

Any hopes of a comeback disappeared within six minutes of the restart. Winsley Boteli doubled Switzerland’s advantage in the 47th minute before Alvyn Sanches produced a superb finish to make it three.

Scotland struggled to recover, with Scott McTominay missing a glorious opportunity to pull one back from close range. The Swiss remained comfortable throughout and added a fourth in the 89th minute when Zeki Amdouni’s effort took a deflection off Luke Graham and beat Angus Gunn.

Singapore vs Brazil - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (701 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Freddie Cotton | 15 Nov 2026 23:35.
  • Singapore welcome Brazil to the Singapore National Stadium on Tuesday morning for their final international fixture of the calendar year.
  • In their previous outing, the Lions fell to a damning defeat against Paraguay, while Selecao conceded in additional time to lose 3-2 to Japan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Freddie Cotton | 15 Nov 2026 23:35.

Singapore welcome Brazil to the Singapore National Stadium on Tuesday morning for their final international fixture of the calendar year.

In their previous outing, the Lions fell to a damning defeat against Paraguay, while Selecao conceded in additional time to lose 3-2 to Japan.

After a disappointing ASEAN Championship campaign, bowing out to Thailand in the semi-finals to deny themselves of a first crown in seven tournament editions, Singapore have endured a tough run of results to close out the calendar year.

Having fallen to defeat against Indonesia in their opening ASEAN Cup fixture in September, the Lions did well to bounce back with a narrow victory over Bangladesh, but after suffering a thumping 6-0 loss to Malaysia in their final group match, Gavin Lee’s men failed to qualify for the knockout stages.

Singapore have so far been unsuccessful in their attempt to bounce back during the current international break too, having endured a resounding 4-1 defeat against Paraguay on home soil last week, making it just the two victories in their previous eight outings.

However, facing Brazil for the very first time, the Lions have the opportunity to forget about their recent woes on Tuesday morning by claiming a historic victory against Selecao, in what would be the highest-ranked FIFA opposition the hosts have ever overcome.

Following last year’s mediocre World Cup qualification campaign, in which they finished fifth out of 10 South American nations and squeezing through to the competition finals, Brazil will undoubtedly be underwhelmed with how they performed in the summer’s tournament.

Despite concluding the group stage at the summit of the Group C table, pipping Morocco to top spot on goal difference, and edging past Japan in their first knockout fixture, Selecao’s tournament came to a premature end at the quarterfinal stage as they suffered a convincing 2-0 defeat to Norway.

Much like their opposition, Carlo Ancelotti’s men have failed to fight back from their tournament woes in recent friendlies too as although they have won two of their previous four matches, Brazil have faced much weaker opposition and head into Tuesday’s clash off the back of a disappointing defeat to Japan at the weekend.

If Selecao are to respond quickly, one of their biggest avenues for improvement is their defensive solidity, with Ancelotti’s side keeping just three clean sheets in their previous 14 games and conceding five goals over their latest three matches.

Singapore form (all competitions):.

Brazil form (all competitions):.

Having picked up no fresh injury concerns against Paraguay, Singapore head into Tuesday’s match with a predominantly fit squad, though the hosts are still without defender Nur Abdullah as the 25-year-old continues his recovery from an ACL injury.

After netting the equaliser on Friday, Ui-Young Song is almost certain to start in the Lions’ attack once again against Brazil, likely alongside fellow Lion City Sailors club teammates Farhan Zulkifli and Ilhan Fandi.

Following his red card in the dying stages of Saturday’s clash with Japan, 29-year-old forward Raphinha will be unavailable this week for Brazil, alongside Ancelotti, who will be absent from the sidelines having been sent off just moments later.

In the Barcelona winger’s absence, Ancelotti will be hoping that Vinicius Junior can continue his hot streak for Selecao, having netted both goals in the defeat to the Samurai Blue after a rocky patch to start the season for Real Madrid.

However, the visitors are missing multiple of their big hitters, with Gabriel Martinelli, Joao Pedro and Lucas Paqueta among those to be sidelined and unavailable for Brazil this week.

Singapore possible starting lineup:.

Mahbud; R.Stewart, Harun, Mahler, Baharudin; Nakamura, Shahiran; Zulkifli, H.Stewart, Song; Fandi.

Brazil possible starting lineup:.

Bento; Wesley Franca, Cunha, Gabriel, Carlos Augusto; Guimaraes, Santos, Gomes; Estevao, Endrick, Vinicius Junior.

With Selecao struggling to string a run of form together, Singapore can certainly be forgiven for having aspirations of a giant killing this week, especially on home soil.

However, despite their difficulties, we think Brazil will bounce straight back on Tuesday morning with a convincing victory at the Singapore National Stadium.

#14377. AI’s energy paradox: will the AI boom strain energy systems or be the source of solutions?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1492 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

AI’s energy paradox: will the AI boom strain energy systems or be the source of solutions?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1492 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ginelle Greene-Dewasmes is working to make AI energy use more sustainable.
  • Artificial intelligence is exploding in popularity, and many people have concerns about the sustainability of its energy consumption.
  • Industry observers note that however, AI might also hold the key to improving energy efficiency: offsetting some of the demand it creates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ginelle Greene-Dewasmes is working to make AI energy use more sustainable.

Artificial intelligence is exploding in popularity, and many people have concerns about the sustainability of its energy consumption. AI models need vast amounts of electricity: according to the International Energy Agency, a typical AI data centre can consume as much energy as 100,000 households each year. Energy use by US data-centre servers more than tripled between 2014 and 2023 — reaching 4.4% of the nation’s total electricity consumption. This figure is expected to at least double by 20281.

Industry observers note that however, AI might also hold the key to improving energy efficiency: offsetting some of the demand it creates. An article published by the World Economic Forum suggests that the use of AI tools across industries — in automating tasks or monitoring real-time energy use, for example — can reduce energy consumption by up to 60%. Ginelle Greene-Dewasmes, a sustainable-development specialist and an author of the article, has been working to lower AI’s energy demands while finding ways to use the tools to reduce wider emissions.

Originally from Trinidad, Greene-Dewasmes became interested in solving energy-security complications for island states with few resources. In 2021, she completed a PhD on the green-energy transition across small island developing states at the University of York, UK, before joining the World Economic Forum in 2022. Now based in Geneva, Switzerland, Greene-Dewasmes has been the Forum’s AI and Energy Lead since 2024. Her work involves bringing together AI and energy leaders from around the world to identify shared challenges, align priorities and develop practical actions that can improve AI’s energy impact.

As well as looking at improving AI’s energy efficiency, Greene-Dewasmes and partners are exploring how models can find innovations that improve existing energy infrastructure, such as that in buildings that are already in use. Nature spoke to her about navigating the increasing energy needs of the technology and whether its benefits could outweigh this demand.

Sources indicate that AI needs cloud networks, chips, graphics-processing units and cooling systems, all of which consume large amounts of energy. Developing and training models requires high levels of processing power to crunch the data, but AI use is much more energy intensive overall because of the scale. ChatGPT, the chatbot from technology firm OpenAI in San Francisco, California, has more than 800 million customers each month and receives more than 2.5 billion queries daily. As AI becomes mainstream, we need to build more energy infrastructure to keep up with the surge in demand.

In a recent development, but, when it comes to scaling up AI, I think the conversation is too skewed towards the energy needed to power centralized infrastructure, when there are lots of other things that will contribute to AI’s energy requirements. Large data centres will exist in only the few countries that have the money, space and resources to host them. For most of the world, AI infrastructure will be disaggregated and decentralized. For example, if one million people are using their phones more intensively because of AI, that affects the energy infrastructure.

According to recent reports, although more complex LLM queries are currently directed to remote data centres, some smaller tasks can be completed directly on latest devices that have AI chips. As this becomes more common, what will that mean for infrastructure planning for energy? It’s much harder to measure this than the outputs from one data centre.

Sources indicate that AI’s electricity impact is at the moment about 0.49% of total global electricity use — so it’s still fairly small, although it’s growing. The World Economic Forum, in collaboration with other specialists, has created a Net-Positive AI Energy Framework. It looks at how we can design AI models and infrastructure for efficiency — by optimizing chips, data-centre locations and liquid cooling, in which fluids are used for cooling owing to their high heat capacity — while using AI to bring down energy usage in high-impact sectors, such as transportation and urbanization, both by improving the efficiency of systems and coming up with solutions to global challenges.

In a recent development, for example, in Azerbaijan, operations that keep buildings running, including lighting, heating and cooling, account for a large proportion of the country’s carbon emissions. The Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution Azerbaijan (a public legal entity) is using AI-powered solutions to improve efficiencies as part of its nationally determined contribution commitments — the country’s pledge to reduce emissions. This includes AI solutions that adjust heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) on the basis of building occupancy and use trends, and that predict the need for maintenance before faults arise. In some cases, this use of AI to hone efficiency has brought down HVAC energy use by 25% and emissions by up to 40%.

We’re also encouraging people to use AI wisely. We want AI to reduce energy consumption overall, rather than adding strain to systems.

Recent findings suggest that the aim is to gather insights from leading voices in the AI ecosystem to generate thought leadership and encourage cross-discipline learning so people aren’t working in silos. It started off as one-on-one conversations with professionals working with AI, centred on the technology’s biggest challenges and opportunities. We convened a community of about 40 people, which has increased to around 70 in nine industries around the world and is still growing. We try to hear from lots of voices: university academics, public-sector entities and technology, AI and energy companies (including renewables and nuclear) are all involved. Together with our partners, we turn these insights into guidance and frameworks that can support the wider industry.

Industry observers note that we’ve published two reports based on the learnings gleaned from these thought leaders. Artificial Intelligence Energy Paradox explores how to balance the challenges and opportunities of AI and energy. The Net-Positive AI Energy Framework is our North Star for clean, efficient and equitable AI. We’re now working on an AI Energy Readiness Compass: a methodology to support responsible AI energy developments and identify the causes of upcoming bottlenecks in the power grid that could be problematic for AI energy use.

Industry observers note that one particular success from these collaborations is the willingness of hyperscalers — large organizations that operate cloud computing services and data centres — to embrace grid flexibility. At first, they were reluctant to adjust when they draw power because they wanted continuous access to reliable electricity, but they have come to see the benefits of balancing demand on the grid. As a result, they have embraced power flexibility, and 18 partners supported the launch of the AI Energy Management Alliance: a coalition of companies that promotes dynamic load-shifting (changing when energy is used to align with grid loads, the availability of green energy and the best pricing).

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03412-5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andy Robertson issued a warning that Scotland do not have time to get things right under Sebastien Pocognoli after his record-breaking night was spoiled by a 4-0 defeat in Switzerland.

The Tottenham left-back became Scotland’s most-capped player by making his 103rd appearance in St Gallen to eclipse the previous milestone of 102 caps set by Kenny Dalglish 40 years ago.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, the captain’s personal achievement was overshadowed by a dismal performance and result that left Scotland with a record of seven points from a possible 18 and a third place finish in Nations League Group B1.

Switzerland were gifted a first-half opener when Lewis Ferguson turned a harmless cross into his own net before Scotland allowed the roof to cave in by conceding twice in the opening six minutes of the second half.

Strikes from Winsley Boteli and Alvyn Sanches put the hosts 3-0 up before Zeki Amdouni added a fourth in the final minute to increase scrutiny on Pocognoli after a less than impressive start to his tenure.

It has been revealed that "I thought first half we were in the game," Robertson mentioned. "We lost a stupid goal but I thought we had chances and could easily have been one-each at half-time.

"We talk about it at half-time to say keep going and by 50 minutes we're 3-0 down. That cannot happen in international football.

According to recent reports, "We were playing against a good team but we were in the game in the first half. We have to do it for 90 minutes. Then you're 3-0 down at a tough place. A really tough night for us.".

Pocognoli has yet to convince the Tartan Army that he is the right appointment after succeeding Steve Clarke, who resigned after seven years in charge following Scotland's World Cup exit.

In a recent development, asked if it will take time for the 39-year-old Belgian's methods to bear fruit, Robertson warned: "I don't think you've got time in international football. You have to do it.

It has been revealed that "Are those supporters who have travelled everywhere going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden that are going to be critical, and rightly so, going to give us time? No. We've not got time. The players don't have time. We have to step up.

"We now have a long break until March which is not a good thing. It's going to be a tough one to swallow.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scotland midfielder John McGinn has warned his international teammates not to hide behind fans’ formation frustrations after pressure mounted on head coach Sebastian Pocognoli following a 4-0 defeat to Switzerland.
  • McGinn, 31, was powerless to resist as Scotland’s poor Nations League campaign ended in a dismal defeat against a heavily rotated Switzerland side.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland midfielder John McGinn has warned his international teammates not to hide behind fans’ formation frustrations after pressure mounted on head coach Sebastian Pocognoli following a 4-0 defeat to Switzerland.

McGinn, 31, was powerless to resist as Scotland’s poor Nations League campaign ended in a dismal defeat against a heavily rotated Switzerland side. A Lewis Ferguson own goal opened the scoring early on, before second half strikes from Winsley Boteli, Alvyn Sanchez and Zeki Amdouni saw the hosts coast to victory in St Gallen.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A third defeat in Pocognoli’s first six games, the result meant Scotland ended their Group B1 campaign in an underwhelming third place, leaving many supporters frustrated by Pocognoli’s refusal to turn away from a rigid 3-4-2-1 formation, with some believing that he is struggling to adapt his tactics to fit the strengths of the squad.

However, Aston Villa captain McGinn has refused to blame Pocognoli, insisting that formations and the newly introduced manager’s methods become irrelevant if the players aren’t displaying their qualities on the pitch.

Sources indicate that “Obviously the trajectory of results means it’s impossible for me to say yes,” stated McGinn when asked if Scotland are on the right path. “But we have been here before, and unfortunately we’ve been in moments where you need to stick together, show your qualities. Players need to come into the group and add more. And you need to turn results around, which we have shown before.

“The manager can’t kick the ball for us. It’s up to us to make the right decisions in those moments, execute it, show a bit of quality, and be a lot better on the ball and off the ball. And that doesn’t matter what tactics you have or formation you play, you need to be a lot better in yourself and not a lot of us can say that tonight.”.

Industry observers note that the 4-0 hammering was Scotland’s final game of the calendar year, with the team not due to play again until their European Championship 2028 qualifying campaign begins in March. Desperate to qualify for their third successive Euros, McGinn set out a plan of attack for the upcoming year and insists the best way for the squad to support Pocognoli is by improving their performances on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve qualified for three out of four major tournaments,” mentioned McGinn. “If we’re going to qualify for a fourth, we need to be much better, We know that. We know what it takes, but you don’t have time in football as a bunch of players to do that. So, come March, we need to be a lot better and improve.”.

Meanwhile, Pocognoli defended the performance against the Swiss, and insisted the scoreline did not reflect the action on the pitch, saying: “The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don’t think it’s a reflection of the game, if I’m really honest and objective. I think we had some very good moments in the game, we started the game like we wanted, aggressive away from home. We played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments in the game.”.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admits his newlook team need to deliver sooner rather than later

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (767 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a newly introduced style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

In a recent development, asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he mentioned: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

In a recent development, ‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  notes his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'.

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

According to recent reports, ‘Some fresh faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’.

McGinn also stated that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most notable part.

‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’.

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager stated: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’.

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

According to recent reports, but the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli.

‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’.

Latest Update: Kenya vs South Africa - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Nsidibe Akpan | 15 Nov 2026 23:55.
  • Kenya host South Africa in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Group D qualifier at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Tuesday.
  • The return leg arrives four days after substitute Ryan Ogam’s 90th-minute strike earned Harambee Stars a 2-2 draw in Soweto, a result that cut Pitso Mosimane’s lead at the top of the group to a single point over Guinea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 15 Nov 2026 23:55.

Kenya host South Africa in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Group D qualifier at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Tuesday.

The return leg arrives four days after substitute Ryan Ogam’s 90th-minute strike earned Harambee Stars a 2-2 draw in Soweto, a result that cut Pitso Mosimane’s lead at the top of the group to a single point over Guinea.

Kenya have taken two points from three Group D games, drawing 1-1 with Eritrea at Nyayo National Stadium, losing 1-0 away to Guinea and then drawing 2-2 in Soweto.

Qualification for the finals is already secured because Kenya co-host the tournament with Uganda and Tanzania, so only one non-host team from the group will advance and Benni McCarthy’s side are chasing a first win of the campaign rather than a place.

Kenya conceded in all three qualifiers, and the first leg followed the pattern: Amos Wanjala, who started in defensive midfield, sent a heavy backpass into his own net in the ninth minute, Michael Olunga levelled from the penalty spot in the 44th minute after Thabang Matuludi handled, and Ogam struck after Olwethu Makhanya was dispossessed.

McCarthy stated his side struggled with South Africa’s full-backs until he moved to a back three early in the second half, with the wing-backs tasked with occupying them.

He has promised a more aggressive approach at home and pointed to Nairobi’s altitude and climate as conditions his players know and the visitors may not.

Olunga’s penalty was his 35th goal for Kenya, level with William Ouma as the national record scorer, and one more would make him the outright leader less than a week after returning from roughly five months out with a pelvic injury that required surgery in Paris.

Ogam, who plays for RFC Liege, has scored two of Kenya’s three group goals, an 87th-minute equaliser against Eritrea and the late leveller in Soweto, the first open-play goal Kenya have scored against South Africa.

McCarthy, born in Cape Town and South Africa’s record international scorer with 31 goals, was facing his native country as a head coach in a competitive match for the first time, and President William Ruto has urged supporters to fill Nyayo National Stadium for the return.

South Africa arrive in Nairobi with seven points from three games, one ahead of Guinea, after beating Guinea 2-1 and Eritrea 5-0 before the draw in Soweto.

The 2-2 result was the first time Bafana Bafana dropped points since Mosimane returned as head coach, and they led twice without being able to hold on.

Relebohile Mofokeng of Union Saint-Gilloise now has three qualifying goals, two in the 5-0 win over Eritrea and the 77th-minute finish in Soweto that followed a pass from substitute Lyle Foster.

Mosimane’s side have scored nine and conceded three in three games, and both Kenya goals in Soweto came from defensive lapses, with Matuludi’s handball giving away the penalty and Makhanya failing to clear before Ogam won the ball.

Mbekezeli Mbokazi, who missed the wins over Guinea and Eritrea with a thigh injury, is available again after being left out of the first-leg XI, and Makhanya is the obvious player to make way.

South Africa have never lost to Kenya in normal time, with three wins and a 1-1 draw in four previous friendlies, although Kenya won the 2002 penalty shootout that followed that draw.

Mosimane remarked the squad took the first available flight to Nairobi, leaving at 01:00 on Saturday and landing at around 06:00, and that no player reported fatigue when the group trained on Sunday.

Kenya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

South Africa Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

South Africa form (all competitions):.

Kenya have no suspensions reported, and Olunga and defender Eric Ouma are back after long injury layoffs, with Ouma used as a substitute in Soweto.

Wrexham defender Zak Vyner was left out of the first leg because of a paperwork problem, and McCarthy said he was hopeful that it would be resolved in time for Tuesday, which would allow the uncapped 29-year-old to make his debut.

Olunga was replaced by Micah Obiero in the second half in Soweto, so the captain’s match fitness is the main selection question, while Ogam is pushing for a start after coming off the bench to score.

Byrne Odhiambo, Frank Odhiambo, Sylvester Owino, Abud Omar and Rooney Onyango all started in the first leg, and McCarthy used Wanjala in midfield before moving him into a back three.

For South Africa, Mosimane has the full squad available, with no suspensions, although centre-backs Ime Okon and Makhanya each carry one yellow card and a second caution would rule them out of their next qualifier.

Goalkeeper Ronwen Williams and midfielder Teboho Mokoena were fitness doubts after missing Mamelodi Sundowns matches, yet both started in Soweto, while Thapelo Maseko missed the squad through injury and Themba Zwane and Nkosinathi Sibisi were left out.

Williams will want to bounce back after Olunga sent him the wrong way from the spot, a penalty McCarthy highlighted because the goalkeeper is regarded as one of the best penalty stoppers in Africa.

Up front, Oswin Appollis, Tshepang Moremi and Iqraam Rayners started in Soweto, with Foster and Puso Dithejane replacing Moremi and Rayners in the second half and lifting the side.

Kenya possible starting lineup:.

B. Odhiambo; Wanjala, F. Odhiambo, Owino; Omar, Tera, J. Ochieng, R. Onyango; Wilson, Olunga, Ogam.

South Africa possible starting lineup:.

Williams; Matuludi, Mbokazi, Okon, Modiba; Sithole, Mokoena; Appollis, Mofokeng, Moremi; Foster.

South Africa have the sharper attack, with nine goals in three games against Kenya’s three, and Mofokeng, Appollis and Moremi should find space on the flanks if McCarthy follows through on his promise to push higher up the pitch.

Kenya’s counter-argument is strong, because the back-three adjustment worked in Soweto, Nairobi’s altitude is a real factor, and Olunga needs one goal to hold the national scoring record outright.

Even so, Kenya have conceded in all three qualifiers and have not kept a clean sheet, while Mosimane can restore Mbokazi to fix the problem that cost his side two points.

A team that has twice squandered a lead should respond with more control, and South Africa’s depth up front should be enough to take a narrow win, with Olunga or Ogam likely to give Kenya a consolation.

💡 Key Takeaways
