  • Today's UEFA Nations League predictions include a battle for top spot in League A Group 2, with Germany taking on Netherlands, while Greece are looking to take three points against Serbia to keep their hopes of finishing in the top two alive.
  • Faroe Islands play host to Moldova on Monday night looking for the win that would see them finish in second place in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ellis Stevens | 16 Nov 2026 00:00.

Today's UEFA Nations League predictions include a battle for top spot in League A Group 2, with Germany taking on Netherlands, while Greece are looking to take three points against Serbia to keep their hopes of finishing in the top two alive.

Faroe Islands play host to Moldova on Monday night looking for the win that would see them finish in second place in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.

However, the visitors only require a draw to ensure that they qualify for the promotion playoffs.

In a recent development, after their surprise draw in Slovakia, Faroe Islands will be full of confidence for this contest. However, Moldova are on their own high, and we feel that the visitors to Torshavn will do enough to earn the share of the spoils that they require for second place.

According to recent reports, > Faroe Islands vs. Moldova preview.

Slovakia square off against Kazakhstan on Monday having already secured top spot in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.

In sharp contrast to the visitors earning promotion with a game to spare, Kazakhstan must win this fixture to have any chance of avoiding finishing bottom of the group.

Slovakia will be motivated to retain their unbeaten record in the group, leading us to back the visitors to avoid defeat. Nevertheless, Kazakhstan perform better on familiar territory than on their travels, so a low-scoring draw could play out.

> Kazakhstan vs. Slovakia preview.

Lithuania welcome Liechtenstein to the Darius and Girenas Stadium on Monday evening for the final round of League D fixtures in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Trispalves fell to a narrow 1-0 defeat against Azerbaijan, while Blau-Rot lost to Milli Komanda by the same scoreline on Friday evening.

With nothing to lose, Liechtenstein will be gunning to end their Nations League campaign on a high and claim their first victory over Lithuania in 15 years.

However, facing a Trispalves side who have lost just one of their previous five matches and took all three points when the nations met in September, it is difficult to see that happening and we predict the hosts to confirm a second-placed finish by winning on Monday evening.

> Lithuania vs. Liechtenstein preview.

Estonia will welcome Bulgaria to the Lillekula Stadium in Tallinn for Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The hosts, who have secured a top-two finish, could still achieve automatic promotion, while the visitors only have pride to play for on the final matchday of the league phase.

Estonia have proven to be a tough team to break down in Group C4, and considering Bulgaria have failed to score in three of their last four games, we think the hosts could edge a cagey contest on Monday.

Iceland will look to wrap up automatic promotion when they welcome Luxembourg to Reykjavik for Monday's Nations League encounter.

The hosts are sitting two points at the top of Group C4, while the visitors are languishing at the bottom of the standings ahead of the final matchday of the league phase.

Iceland will be full of confidence after thrashing Bulgaria 5-0 last time out, and we think they will produce another free-scoring display against a Luxembourg side that are low on confidence after four consecutive defeats.

Industry observers note that > Iceland vs. Luxembourg preview.

Gibraltar will be looking to finish their UEFA Nations League campaign on a positive note when they welcome Malta to Europa Point Stadium on Monday evening.

The visitors have already secured top spot in their League D group, while the hosts will be keen to pick up their first win.

Gibraltar should provide a tough test for Malta, but the visitors are unbeaten in the Nations League for a reason and should have enough quality to pick up the win.

Switzerland welcome Scotland to Berit Sitterstadion on Monday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League League B Group 1.

The hosts have already secured top spot heading into the final game, while the visitors are still battling to finish second and in the promotion playoff place.

Scotland may have more at stake but Switzerland have been the dominant force in League B Group 1, and we expect their unbeaten run to continue with another win here.

Sources indicate that > Switzerland vs. Scotland preview.

North Macedonia will welcome Slovenia to Tose Proeski Arena on Monday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League B Group 1.

The hosts' relegation to League C has already been confirmed, while the visitors are fighting to secure second place and a chance at promotion to League A.

Slovenia are undoubtedly the favourites to win this match, as demonstrated in their comfortable victory in the reverse fixture, and the visitors should secure all three points.

It has been revealed that > North Macedonia vs. Slovenia preview.

Fighting for a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Germany are set to host League A's Group A2 leaders, the Netherlands, at Olympiastadion Berlin on Monday.

Die Mannschaft know that they likely need to win to progress, while Oranje are through barring an unprecedented swing in goal-difference.

The maths of the table may be complex, but Germany know that a simple victory will see them through to the quarter-finals.

Oranje have yet to lose in the Nations League this season, though with the stakes lowered, they could be caught off guard.

Industry observers note that > Germany vs. Netherlands preview.

Under pressure in League A of the UEFA Nations League, Greece will welcome Serbia to Panthessaliko Stadium for their final Group A2 showdown on Monday.

The Azure and White are battling for a place in the quarter-finals, while the Eagles are competing to earn a place in the League A/B playoffs.

Greece may have been hammered 7-0 by the Netherlands last time out, but that defeat came as a shock, and with a place in the quarter-finals at stake, the hosts will be motivated to bounce back.

Serbia have struggled throughout this term's Nations League, and it would be surprising to see them avoid a sixth consecutive defeat on Monday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic have been hailed as the perfect destination for England international Jadon Sancho to reignite his career and shine again as he continues the search for his next club.

Recent findings suggest that sancho, 26, is presently a free agent after his contract at Manchester United expired in the summer, but was part of the Aston Villa squad that won the Europa League with a 3-0 win over Freiburg after spending last season on-loan in the Midlands. He also won the Conference League with Chelsea in the previous campaign.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A £73million signing for Manchester United in the summer of 2021, Sancho was viewed as one of Europe’s most promising talents during his time at Borussia Dortmund, scoring 50 goals in 137 appearances and forming a lethal partnership with former Signal Iduna favourites Marco Reus, Erling Haaland, and Jude Bellingham.

Sources indicate that however, the pacey winger was never able to replicate his Dortmund form at Old Trafford, culminating in a high-profile public fallout with former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag over training performances in September 2023. Sancho spent the following three seasons away on loan from the club before being released, but he’s now been urged to consider Celtic as his next destination by former Parkhead icon Paul Lambert.

Recent findings suggest that “Jadon Sancho to Celtic? You could see something like that working,” Lambert told BetVictor. “I don't think he should have left Dortmund for Man United. I thought he should have stayed, like Jude did. Like I remarked, I don't think Jude Bellingham would be the player he is if he'd stayed in Britain. He made that move to Borussia Dortmund and propelled himself. I think his brother Jobe is the same, a terrific young player.

In a recent development, “Leaving Britain to play in Germany at Borussia Dortmund was the right decision. Would Harry Kane have won the Ballon d'Or if he was still at Tottenham? Absolutely no chance. He went to a club with incredible standards and a great league, and it propelled him. I'd argue with anyone until I'm blue in the face, would Jude Bellingham be the player he is if he went straight from Birmingham to Real Madrid?

Recent findings suggest that “Absolutely no chance. Borussia Dortmund gave him the platform, and Jobe is the same. I saw him play against Bayern Munich at the weekend and he was excellent. Moving abroad makes you grow up, and if you pick the right club, your game improves tenfold. Looking back at Jadon going to Man United at that point, I would have stayed in Dortmund.

“As long as Jadon gets his creative head back on, because he's definitely a threat when he has the ball. He's got to get that back. You could see it happening, and he wouldn't be adverse to it as long as he has the fire and hunger, because he has the ability. He just has to pick the right club to give him that platform to express himself again, that could be Celtic.”.

The midfielder’s 21st minute spot-kick, converted after Charlie Hester-Cook had been fouled by the Gulls’ Caleb Roberts, proved to be the difference between the two National League South rivals at the Fusion Aviation Community Stadium on Saturday.

In an end-to-end Trophy tie, the Hornets hit the woodwork three times in the first half and had plenty of opportunities in the second.

Torquay saw a fine effort superbly saved by Horsham stopper Sam Howes before clattering the crossbar – but the hosts held on to advance to the third round.

The Hornets will host Isthmian North outfit Hashtag United in the next round, which will be played on Saturday, December 12.

Horsham visit Dover Athletic in National League South this Saturday before welcoming Truro City on Tuesday, November 24.

Latest Update: Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino faces battle for 'impressive' £21m centre-back from Liverpool and Chelsea

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (333 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 00:21.
  • Manchester United share interest in AC Milan defender Koni De Winter with Liverpool and Chelsea, the newest report has claimed.
  • The Red Devils are preparing for the return of Premier League football, with Mauricio Pochettino set to take charge of his first game on November 22 against Liverpool.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 00:21.

Manchester United share interest in AC Milan defender Koni De Winter with Liverpool and Chelsea, the newest report has claimed.

The Red Devils are preparing for the return of Premier League football, with Mauricio Pochettino set to take charge of his first game on November 22 against Liverpool.

There are concerns that his weak defence could cost the newly introduced head coach at Anfield, with the likes of Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez having struggled this season.

Recruiting new defenders should be seen as a priority, and it should come as no surprise to see the club linked with a host of talented stars.

Tuttomercatoweb report that United hold serious interest in AC Milan centre-back De Winter, who is valued by Transfermarkt at just under £21m, though they may face competition from the likes of Liverpool and Chelsea.

Pochettino is known to use an aggressive system, with the 54-year-old often asking defenders to step forward and press from the halfway line.

De Winter possesses immense speed, and the 24-year-old is far more mobile then any of United's current options at the back.

The Belgian has been trusted on the ball by Milan, with the centre-back so far averaging 61.1 successful passes per game in Serie A.

De Winter also wins most of his battles in the air, and he could be a sensible addition in either January or the summer.

Both Liverpool and Chelsea will almost certainly qualify for European competitions this season, whereas United are fighting a relegation battle.

However, the Reds may not need to sign a centre-back if Virgil van Dijk extends his stay beyond this summer, though the Blues are always active in the market.

Pochettino may find it hard to convince De Winter to join, especially if Chelsea secure either Champions League or Europa League football, and it remains to be seen if Old Trafford will still be the attraction it once was for transfer targets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Celtic and Hibs head coach Tony Mowbray has been forced to step down from his role at EFL Championship outfit Blackburn Rovers due to health complications.

Mowbray, 62, returned to the dugout at Ewood Park for a second time in the summer, having previously managed the club between 2017 and 2022, where he led Blackburn to 13th in the table after winning six of his first 15 games in charge of the club.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, in an emotional statement on the club’s official website, Mowbray has now confirmed he has departed his role as manager, with assistant Mike Dodds placed in temporary charge.

Previously head coach at Birmingham City, he stepped away from his role at St Andrew’s in early 2024 due to health reasons, later revealing he had been undergoing treatment for bowel cancer, though he was eventually given the all-clear following treatment.

A statement on Blackburn’s website read: “Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers. I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them.

Recent findings suggest that “Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you've given me. It's been a pleasure working alongside you. To the fans, thank you for the way you've supported me and the team this season. I've always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.".

In response, Blackburn chief executive officer Steve Curwood said: “Tony's passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he shows for players, staff and those around him that mean so much. Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.”.

It has been revealed that during his successful management career, Mowbray led West Bromwich Albion and Blackburn to promotion and, more recently, took Sunderland to the EFL Championship playoffs in 2023. At Hibs, he won the Scottish Football Writers' Association manager of the year award, spending two years at Easter Road between 2004 and 2006.

Sources indicate that he returned to the Scottish Premiership with Celtic, whom he represented over 75 times during his playing career in the summer of 2009. However, a lack of domestic success saw him relieved of his duties the following March.

Worthing enter the competition at the next stage along with all their National League Premier counterparts – and it is one of them, Forest Green Rovers, who they will welcome to Woodside Road for the tie.

The Rebels are at the moment nine places above Rovers in the table but lost 2-1 at home to them in Woodside Road’s first ever game at step one in August so weill be out to put that right – along with the memory of FGR’s FA Cup win at Worthing last October in the first game after Adam Hinshelwood returned to the dugout.

Industry observers note that horsham have been drawn at home to Hashtag United – a side who now play two divisions below the Hornets. Hashtag are plying their trade in the Isthmian North division this season after relegation from step three last season and are doing well – sitting third at present.

But after Dominic Di Paola’s side put out Torquay in round two on Saturday with an excellent 1-0 victory, they will start as favourites in the next round.

Only one of the surviving Sussex trio are on the road – Eastbourne Borough are off to Oxford City, who play one step above the sports in National League North.

Borough reached the next round with a last-gasp Tyano Wilson winner that saw them beat Chertsey 2-1 at Priory Lane on Saturday.

There’s plenty of incentive for all teams taking part in the third round – winners at that stage pick up £4,500 prize money, with losers receiving £1,250 each.

Victory also puts teams into the last 32 (fourth round) – when dreams of Wembley might start to take shape.

Ties in round three are due to take place on Saturday, December 12.

Missing out on a third round spot are Chichester City, Burgess Hill and Whitehawk, who all lost their second round ties at the weekend.

Worthing Women: Make Mackay-ne a double!

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicole Mackay’s brace made it three goals in two games for her and a second successive win for Worthing Women, as they saw off Aylesford at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium.

After last week’s epic cup comeback at Camden, teenage starlet Hattie Rainey made her full debut while Ruby Murdock also came into the starting eleven; meaning that Skye Birkinshaw and Cristie Pritchard began on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Barely had supporters sat in their seats than the aforementioned Mackay got the home team off and running, just three minutes in.

Seizing on  a loose ball on the edge of the eighteen yard area, the in-form striker drilled low and hard into Aylesford ‘keeper Sade Rider’s bottom right-hand corner, to open the scoring in emphatic fashion.

Although a very different picture might have been painted had the Rebels's netminder Sian Woods not denied a clean through Leigha Bradding-Butler not once but twice, to deny the visitor’s top scorer a seventh strike of a prolific campaign.

Still inside the opening ten minutes, Mackay came the width of the crossbar away from extending the host’s advantage. Dusting herself down and stepping up to take a free-kick she herself had won, the ball cannoned back off the frame of the goal, with Jess Richardson landing the rebound on top of the net.

The game settled into a more even contest for some time after that, as Worthing pressed forward in search of a second before the break, with Aylesford looking dangerous on the counter-attack.

Approaching the half-time interval, an audible sigh of relief reverberated around Woodside Road via Immy Armstrong - a threat from her set-pieces - firing narrowly over the target from inside the penalty area.

The sun then broke through the clouds on a pleasant November afternoon; similar to the way in which Aliyah Sheridan did when gifted possession by the homester’s otherwise solid last line of defence. Woods redeemed herself via a strong parry to her left of Sheridan’s subsequent shot.

One final opportunity before the change of ends fell to visiting Skipper Ami Burnham, only for Woods to keep her out by way of another excellent stop.

It’s tight at the bottom of the London & South East Prem but it was the Reds who headed into the interval with a precious one-goal lead.

Recent findings suggest that worthing continued to probe and were rewarded just shy of the hour mark, thanks to the persistence of Mackay. Although it was centre-half Ella Terry who got the ball rolling, courtesy of a wonderful switch of play from the middle of the park out to the roving Richardson on the right flank. The winger then found a well-placed Mackay to test Rider in the travellers’ net, with the Kent club’s custodian unable to prevent the Rebel’s number nineteen from overtaking Amber Hazlewood as leading markswoman in a red (occasionally lilac) shirt.

Some fine build-up laid the foundations for a possible third not long afterwards, when a Hattie Rainey pass went from a central position to wide on the right again, releasing the rapid Richardson to, ultimately, find Mackay once more, with the forward teeing up Neve McEvaddy for a long-range piledriver which saw Rider pull off a terrific save.

Goalscorer nearly turned provider three-quarters of the way into the contest but neither Richardson nor Annie Gracey could apply the finishing  touch to a dangerous-looking delivery.

Almost instantly, the visiting Blues hit back via a neat move of their own, culminating in half-time substitute Kara Richardson forcing Woods to hold on.

Ten to go and another excellent long ball from Terry resulted in some equally impressive hold-up play by the recently-introduced Paige Baker-Carroll, providing Richardson with an opening that she couldn’t quite keep down.

Not over the line yet though, the home side were reminded of the threat carried by Aylesford when Bradding-Bulter’s corner eventually led to Kara Richardson drawing a one-handed stop out of Woods, at the (in)expense of another flag-kick.

Time was running out for the girls from the Garden of England and Armstrong was quick to pounce on Pritchard's pass to fellow replacement Megan Gates; although the final flourish from twenty yards failed to test Woods between the home posts.

Fittingly, Worthing’s brightly-clad netminder had the last word on proceedings, as she added to her collection of wonder saves by frustrating Sheridan with only a few short minutes of normal time to play.

That would, indeed, be that and three vital points stayed at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium to move the Rebels up to ninth in the table, ahead of another tough test at bottom-of-the-table and fellow Sussex side Eastbourne Borough next Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 16 Nov 2026 00:29, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 03:27.

Japan and Paraguay will conclude their respective 2026 schedules when they face off in Tuesday's friendly in Singapore.

The Samurai Blue pulled off a thrilling win over Brazil last time out, while Paraguay cruised to a commanding victory over Singapore in their most recent outing.

Japan head into Tuesday's fixture in fine form, having lost just one of their previous 16 internationals.

Their only defeat in that period came in the Round of 32 tie against Brazil at the 2026 World Cup, which saw them spurn a leading position in a narrow 2-1 defeat.

After conceding a late winner in that contest, Hajime Moriyasu's side managed to exact an element of revenge with a stoppage-time winner of their own in Saturday's friendly against Brazil.

The Samurai Blue looked to have wasted another strong position after Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura saw their efforts cancelled out by a Vinicius Junior brace, before Coventry City's Tatsuhiro Sakamoto turned the game back in Japan's favour with a 91st-minute goal.

Sakamoto's effort made it two wins in Japan's last three head-to-head meetings with Brazil, while making it five games without defeat since their World Cup elimination.

Japan should fancy their chances of extending their unbeaten run with a win, having won four of their previous five meetings with Paraguay (D1) since losing on penalties in the last 16 of the 2010 World Cup.

After eventually being eliminated in the quarter-finals in 2010, Paraguay had to wait 16 years until their next appearance in football's biggest tournament.

La Albirroja certainly made an impact at the 2026 World Cup, advancing to the knockout rounds before eliminating Germany on penalties in the Round of 32.

However, their run ultimately came to an end in a feisty last-16 clash against France, with Kylian Mbappe's 70th-minute penalty proving decisive as Paraguay fell to a narrow 1-0 loss.

Gustavo Alfaro's side have since made a positive return to action with three consecutive wins against Bolivia, Colombia and Singapore.

Gustavo Caballero netted a brace as Paraguay cruised to a 4-1 success in their most recent outing against Singapore, representing just the third time La Albirroja have scored two or more goals in 2026.

Their strength has ultimately been at the opposite end of the pitch, having conceded more than one goal in just two of their 11 games in the current calendar year.

As for Paraguay, Alfaro is expected to make wholesale changes after naming an experimental XI for the win over Singapore.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Industry observers note that matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Industry observers note that matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

It has been revealed that as for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the newly introduced arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

Recent findings suggest that the 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

#14325. New culprit in early Alzheimer’s: blood–brain barrier blocks protective proteins

New culprit in early Alzheimer’s: blood–brain barrier blocks protective proteins

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers tagged dozens of proteins that can cross the blood-brain barrier and are important for brain health.Credit: K.
  • Industry observers note that for decades, scientists thought of the blood–brain barrier as an impenetrable layer.
  • The team also found that the transport of some of these crucial proteins breaks down in mice with brain diseases that mimic early-stage Alzheimer’s disease.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers tagged dozens of proteins that can cross the blood-brain barrier and are important for brain health.Credit: K. H. Fung/SPL.

Industry observers note that for decades, scientists thought of the blood–brain barrier as an impenetrable layer. Over time that view has changed, as researchers realized the barrier was more permeable than first thought. Now, a team have catalogued almost 100 proteins that can pass through it to maintain brain health1.

The team also found that the transport of some of these crucial proteins breaks down in mice with brain diseases that mimic early-stage Alzheimer’s disease.

According to recent reports, “The paradigm in the field has been that the blood–brain barrier is normally impermeable and then becomes leaky as a result of Alzheimer’s disease,” says study co-author Andrew Yang, a neuroscientist at Gladstone Institute of Neurological Disease in San Francisco, California. Instead, his team’s work suggests that the blood–brain barrier actively imports proteins that the brain needs to function and the loss of these proteins drives the dysfunction seen early in the disease, he adds.

According to recent reports, yang and his colleagues developed a technique to label a large array of proteins in the blood and track those that can enter the brain. Of the 861 proteins they mapped, 92 crossed the blood–brain barrier into the brain. Most of these proteins were produced in distant organs, particularly the liver.

The team focused on apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1), which has been linked to potential protective effects against Alzheimer’s disease2. Once inside the brain, APOA1 stimulates brain cells called astrocytes to release cholesterol, which is important for maintaining the synapses through which neurons communicate. But how the protein crossed the blood–brain barrier has been unclear until now, says Yang.

Industry observers note that his team found that two receptors for APOA1 — SR-B1 and ABCA1 — are present on the blood–brain barrier as well as astrocytes. This suggests how the protein moves from the blood–brain barrier to the specific brain cells that need them, the authors say.

When Yang’s team blocked the ABCA1 receptor in laboratory-grown astrocytes, the protein no longer had the same cholesterol-regulating effects.

In a recent development, scientists have long known that the blood–brain barrier breaks down as Alzheimer’s advances, letting harmful molecules leak into the brain. Yang’s team found that a different problem emerges first.

Using their labelling technique in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease, the researchers found that the blood–brain barrier stopped importing protective proteins such as APOA1 into the brain before the barrier began to break down. This disruption to the protein transport was accompanied by a loss of neuronal connections, behavioural changes and other early hallmarks of the disease.

Industry observers note that yang and the team wondered whether increasing the supply of APOA1 in the blood might help to counter some of the damage caused by Alzheimer’s disease. To find out, the team engineered mice with Alzheimer’s to produce extra APOA1 in the liver. When more APOA1 crossed the blood–brain barrier and entered the brain, the mice highlighted fewer Alzheimer’s-disease-related markers. For example, they had reduced fat build-up in astrocytes and lower levels of inflammatory molecules.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The 2-1 scoreline at the Trafalgar Ground was the same as when the Dockers sailed back from Mid Sussex with all three points in August.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three times Hassocks have lost in the Southern Combination Premier Division so far this season. Two of those defeats have come at the hands of Newhaven.

The 2-1 scoreline at the Trafalgar Ground was the same as when the Dockers sailed back from Mid Sussex with all three points in August. The Robins must be delighted to see the back of Newhaven in the league.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

So often the scourge of Hassocks in the past, Lee Robinson scored both the Dockers goals in the space of seven second half minutes.

Lewis Finney pulled one back with 13 minutes remaining and although the Robins threw the kitchen sink at Newhaven, they were unable to find another way through.

The Dockers defence were outstanding and in particular ex-Hassocks centre back Matt Gunn, who deservedly picked up the host's man-of-the-match award afterwards.

Industry observers note that gunn was also a threat at the other end and had two chances to score twice himself inside the opening three minutes. He first saw a flicked header from a corner sensationally tipped around the post by Ed Cooper.

According to recent reports, that resulted in another corner and although the Robins cleared this one, Newhaven were able to recycle possession and get a delivery from Ezra Roeg into the box. Gunn remained forward and met it with a powerful headed effort just over the bar.

Hassocks were unable to cope with the relentless tempo at which the Dockers had started. A situation summed up when Harry Reed and Tom Sekyere converged rapidly on Jack Troak to snare the ball from him.

The intense press got Tyler Capon in down the right flank for a cross which Cooper and Harvey Blake combined to clear in somewhat unorthodox, acrobatic style to prevent Robinson from having a tap-in.

Troak managed to lead an attack which finally broke the Robins out of their own half. His cross hung up into the middle was met by Dan Perry for a header just over.

Sources indicate that perry was making his Hassocks debut after signing from East Grinstead Town in midweek. The Hitman has netted 11 times this season for the Wasps and looks to be a quality addition.

It has been revealed that dan Turner then saw a shot from the edge of the box blocked by the nether regions of Elliott Bresciani. The defender putting his body on the line was an early sign of the sort of defending Newhaven would deploy to good effect to get them over the line in the second half.

With the Robins now a willing participant in the game, things began to ebb and flow from end-to-end. Capon was millimetres away from connecting with a Reed centre and Cooper did just enough to put off Sekyere into placing a one-on-one wide.

Perry looked the most likely source of goals for Hassocks. He drew a routine save from Jake Rhodes when heading a Harvey Blake cross on target.

Rhodes then pulled off a much more difficult reaction stop at close range when Big Alex Fair delivered and Perry stooped to direct a header across the Dockers goalkeeper.

Cooper saved well at his near post when Matt Feeney-Hill cut inside before Newhaven faded a little in the final 10 minutes of the half, probably because of the speed at which they played the previous 35.

As a result, Hassocks were on top in the period leading into the break. Finney saw a shot blocked by Gunn and some nifty footwork from Fair followed by a clever back heel teed up Omar Abdsami for a shot just a little too high.

The second half was a slow-burner in comparison to the first until Robinson fired the Dockers ahead on 63 minutes. Sekyere hooked a hopeful ball over the top of the Hassocks defence which the veteran forward showed a remarkable turn of pace to latch onto.

It carried Robinson clear of Turner and enabled him to curl a fine finish with his side foot around Cooper and into the far corner.

It has been revealed that newhaven doubled their lead with 70 on the clock after the Robins were unconvincing dealing with a corner. The delivery from Feeney-Hill was only half cleared to the edge of the box, allowing Ross Barclay to return an up-and-under into the area.

Gunn won a flick on and it found the unmarked Robinson, who had taken advantage of a slapdash Hassocks offside line to move front and centre of goal where he volleyed home unmarked.

According to recent reports, half-hearted appeals for the goal to be disallowed were easily dismissed. Robinson had stayed in a legal position, thanks in part to the Robins being completely out of shape.

Hassocks now had no choice but to lay siege on the Newhaven goal. Liam Benson came on as James Westlake changed formation and went with two up front.

It has been revealed that the adjustment helped the Robins. Tall striker Jamie Wilkes put an awkward header wide and Devon Fender rattled the post with a good volley from inside the D.

An excellent move halved the deficit on 77 minutes. Abdsami was patient in waiting for a gap to appear into which he could play a forward pass.

When it came, his ball into the feet of Benson was superbly flicked around the corner by the substitute and into the path of Finney.

The finish from Finney was cool as you like as he picked out the far corner with aplomb to move onto double figures for the season.

Hassocks now had 13 minutes in which to try and find an equaliser. Unfortunately, their shooting from that point on did not match the calmness or precision with which Finney had pulled one back.

In a recent development, finney came closest to providing a leveller on 88. Abdsami crossed and Perry directed a clever downwards header into the penalty box. The arriving Finney met it with a rasping volley which Rhodes somehow flung himself upwards to block.

Bresciani produced an overhead kick to clear the loose ball off the line and prevent Benson putting away the rebound. In a moment which summed the afternoon up really for Hassocks, that clearance gave another chance to Blake.

The Robins captain could only blaze so high as to pose more of a threat to Newhaven Fort all the way up the hill than the Dockers goal.

Other than the quality of the Finney finish, there was one other positive for the Robins to take home at least. Raging Joe Bull made his 300th senior appearance for the club, becoming the first Robin to pass the triple century landmark since Phil Gault a decade ago.

Hassocks: Cooper; Blake, D Turner, Hendy, Bull; Wilkes, Finney; Fair, Abdsami, Troak; Perry.

Subs: Fender, Benson, Budd (used), Croal, Brodie (unused).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that taxi for Sebastien Pocognoli? Or should that be cable car? Scotland suffered in Switzerland on Monday and appear to be on a very slippery slope.

Recent findings suggest that steve Clarke endured two 4-0 defeats in his first five matches in charge so let no one argue that heavy beatings alone are sackable offences. But Pocognoli is sorely aware that he is treading on thin ice in the court of public opinion following a 4-0 drubbing against Switzerland in St Gallen, a gateway to the Alps.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He won’t need to look at the main Tartan Army fans’ forum, where the most visited thread is titled simply: sack him.

In a recent development, the numbers commenting suggests a healthy debate is occurring. Although a few are backing him, or at least who are pointing out that six games is not long enough to judge anyone, they are in the minority.

Of course, a lot of this is the usual ‘look at me and my extreme opinion’ showboating. Heaven knows, there was enough of that on X in the aftermath of Scotland’s latest reversal. Everyone’s an expert. Everyone knew better although, in the case of Pocognoli, maybe they did.

He was told Ben Gannon-Doak isn’t a wing-back and he was told that what is good for a game against North Macedonia might not necessarily be what is required against a team like Switzerland. The double midfield pivot of Lewis Ferguson and Billy Gilmour? Isn’t working. Again, a conclusion many reached at the end of the last window, long before the wretched night in a charming Swiss hamlet. Once known as the capital of embroidery, St Gallen is where things began unstitching very badly indeed for Scotland’s upcoming manager after a heavy and cheerless defeat.

It has been revealed that it was as concerning as it was sore. After all, Switzerland played what their fans explained was a B team and yet still had the game won inside 51 minutes. The "oles" had started. If the Swiss weren’t such a polite lot, we might have been treated to a rendition of: "Are you Liechtenstein in disguise?".

It’s just as well the Nations League format has changed otherwise Scotland could be looking at a relegation play-off against the Faroe Islands – unbeaten in six Nations League games – to avoid demotion to League C.

Scotland are not world beaters but they are better than this. They are better than finishing a distant third in a group where they are ranked seven places higher than the team that did in fact finish in second place: Slovenia. That’s underachievement writ large, whether someone is finding his feet or not. There’s giving a manager time and then there’s expecting the bare minimum.

According to recent reports, no wonder there’s anger. No wonder there’s bemusement at the SFA appearing so beholden to the gospel according to Pocognoli that they have permitted his ideas about tactics to cascade throughout the entire set-up. As Under-21 coach Tony Docherty stated a few weeks ago, his side will be a “mirror image” of the A side. Gadzooks. And further down the chain, including the likes of the Under-15s and Under-16s? All working in the same, uniform way, Docherty confirmed.

According to recent reports, memo to the SFA: stop wasting time arranging friendlies in Boston and start rowing back on this one-size-fits-all formula. It could negatively impact Scottish football for generations. In many people's eyes, Pocognoli is already done after a reign lasting barely 90 days.

Recent findings suggest that getting him out means forking out the compensation fee but it also means telling the phalanx of new coaches – as many as ten have been appointed at various age levels – to ditch the high line, the three defenders and ‘box’ midfield. It means turning Hampden upside down.

Industry observers note that it is, nevertheless, a good time to sack someone. If the international window is prime time for clubs to ditch unwanted managers then surely it’s optimal for an international team to do so now: in this long gap between international matches.

Industry observers note that scotland’s next competitive international could be as long away as next September if they are drawn in a four-team group for the Euros. Pocognoli, who turned 39 just before he took the job, could be in his 40s before Scotland next play a match of consequence.

Industry observers note that of course, there is one very notable looming date: Sunday 6 December. Pocognoli – or at least we must assume at the time of writing that it will be Pocognoli – will be present and correct in the International Convention Centre in Belfast for the draw for Euro 2028 qualifying.

Sources indicate that ian Maxwell, the SFA chief executive, will be beside him to face some no doubt awkward questions. One of them will be, where are Scotland going? Because from this angle, it looks like backwards. They are at risk of being splatted with international football’s biggest custard pie: failing to qualify for a tournament they are co-hosting. Now assured pot three in the draw, it’s possible they miss out.

The post-World Cup malaise might well have been unavoidable. Even with Clarke in charge there would have been a likely drop-off. The natives were already restless. Away from the traffic cone malarkey, away from the baseball and boozing, it’s been a dreadful year for the national team.

Six defeats out of 13 matches and just five wins, the only one of any real worth being the 1-0 victory over Haiti and even that drew criticism for not being comprehensive enough. Three defeats in six Nations League games, two of which came at Hampden, suggests it’s going from bad to worse under Pocognoli.

The SFA have been criticised for milking the summer trip to Massachusetts to the max, with reports of a biennial friendly match being arranged at Fenway Park or elsewhere. A hat tip to Boston’s boys of summer might be acceptable if Maxwell and co invoke the fundamental rule of baseball in relation to Pocognoli: Three strikes and you’re out. They won’t and neither should they.

Three defeats in six matches is not a sacking offence. But an appointment the SFA seemed very pleased with themselves to acknowledge was data-led now looks increasingly at risk of an outage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 16 Nov 2026 00:32.

Bottom-placed Liberia host Cape Verde in a Group K fixture of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying at the Samuel Kanyon Doe Sports Complex in Monrovia on Tuesday.

The first leg in Praia on November 13 finished 4-2 to Cape Verde, which lifted the Blue Sharks to three points in third place in a group where only the top two qualify, left Liberia on zero, and kept Mali on nine points and Rwanda on six above them.

The Lone Stars sit bottom of Group K with no points from three matches, having scored three goals and conceded eight, a goal difference of -5 that leaves them six points behind second-placed Rwanda with nine still available.

Mohammed Adil Erradi, the Belgian-Moroccan appointed on a three-year contract on May 18, has yet to win a competitive match as Liberia coach, and a group calling itself the Concerned Stakeholders for Liberian Football Development demanded his dismissal on October 9, according to the Liberian Observer, citing a salary budgeted at US$98,450 a year.

The campaign opened with a 3-1 defeat in Kigali on September 25, where Sylvanus Nimely scored the only Liberian goal, and four days later Mali won 1-0 at this ground through Martial Tia’s 79th-minute strike after goalkeeper Tommy Songo pulled out of the starting line-up during the warm-up.

In Praia on November 13 Liberia trailed 3-1 after 43 minutes, with Franklin Nyenetue’s 36th-minute equaliser cancelled out two minutes later by a corner-kick header from Dje Tavares, before Ayouba Kosiah converted a stoppage-time penalty to set the final score at 4-2.

Liberia’s back three of Jamal Arago, Sampson Dweh and Emmanuel Fully conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse in the first leg, and the defence has now shipped eight goals in three qualifiers, an average of 2.67 per match.

The head-to-head record leans away from the hosts, as Liberia have lost their last three meetings with Cape Verde (2-1 in Accra on October 7, 2021, 1-0 in Mindelo on October 10, 2021, and 4-2 on November 13), although both of their wins in the series came in Monrovia, 3-0 in July 2000 and 1-0 on June 5, 2011.

A post shared by Liberia Men's National Teams (@lbr_lonestar).

Cape Verde arrive third in Group K on three points with a goal difference of -1 (six scored, seven conceded), and a win in Monrovia would take them to six, level with the total at the moment held by second-placed Rwanda, who host Mali in Kigali at the same 7pm GMT kick-off.

The Blue Sharks drew all three of their World Cup group matches in June (0-0 against Spain, 2-2 against Uruguay and 0-0 against Saudi Arabia) to reach the Round of 32 on their tournament debut, where Argentina beat them 3-2 after extra time on July 3, a 111th-minute own goal from Diney Borges settling it after Deroy Duarte and Sidny Lopes Cabral had pulled Cape Verde level twice.

Bubista then left to coach Moroccan club RS Berkane, and Humberto Bettencourt, his assistant for six years, was promoted on August 19, with his first two qualifiers producing a 3-1 defeat at Mali on September 25 and a 2-1 home defeat to Rwanda on September 29.

Those results extended a winless run to six matches, counting the World Cup (three draws and three defeats), which ended in Praia when Ayoni Santos, Dje Tavares, Dailon Livramento and substitute Derensili Sanches Fernandes scored in the 4-2 win, Bettencourt’s first victory in charge.

Cape Verde have conceded in all three of their qualifiers, seven goals at 2.33 per match, compared with five conceded across four World Cup matches, two of which were clean sheets against Spain and Saudi Arabia.

Bettencourt brought in six players for the double-header, among them David Moreira, Yuran Fernandes, Leandro Andrade, Ieltsin Camoes and Sanches Fernandes, and three of the four scorers in Praia (Santos, Tavares and Sanches Fernandes) were finding the net for the senior side for the first time.

Liberia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Liberia form (all competitions):.

Cape Verde Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Cape Verde form (all competitions):.

Liberia captain Oscar Dorley, the Al-Taawoun midfielder, is out with a hamstring injury and was left out of Erradi’s 24-man squad, while goalkeeper Derrick Julu of Niger Tornadoes was recalled to replace Songo, who has not featured since withdrawing from the Mali line-up on September 29.

Julu replaced Ashley Williams at half time in Praia, and Erradi noted afterwards that Williams, who had played well against Mali, was not at his best, which points to Julu starting in goal on Tuesday.

Nyenetue, who plays for Ranheim, scored the equaliser in Praia and was replaced by William Gibson after 64 minutes with no injury reported.

Without Dorley, Nohan Kenneh and Solomon Tweh are the likeliest holding pairing in a four-man midfield that also used Edward Ledlum and Divine Teah of Slavia Prague, with Sampson Dweh of Viktoria Plzen anchoring the back three.

For the visitors, defender Wagner Pina, who had joined the training camp in Portugal, did not travel to Cape Verde for the first leg, and Bettencourt wished him a quick recovery.

The 26-man squad named on November 4 includes Vozinha, 40, defenders Logan Costa and Lopes Cabral, midfielder Jamiro Monteiro and 36-year-old captain Ryan Mendes, although Lopes Cabral was replaced at half time in Praia by Steven Moreira and the reason has not been given.

Bettencourt could keep the 4-1-4-1 that scored four in Praia, with Deroy Duarte shielding the back four, and he used all five substitutions there (Moreira, Monteiro, Laros Duarte, Sanches Fernandes and Camoes), which leaves a bench that is already familiar with the strategy.

Liberia possible starting lineup:.

Julu; Fully, Dweh, Jamal, Nimely; Ledlum, Tweh, Kenneh, Nyenetue; Teah, Kosiah.

Cape Verde possible starting lineup:.

Sources indicate that vozinha; J. Paulo, Diney, Costa, L. Cabral; D. Duarte; Mendes, Tavares, Santos, Varela; Livramento.

The first leg showed where this tie will be decided, as Liberia conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse inside 43 minutes, and with Dorley absent and Erradi having already changed goalkeepers at half time, he has fewer ways to repair that in four days than Bettencourt has to exploit it again.

Liberia deserve credit for scoring twice in Praia and for restricting Mali to a 79th-minute winner on the synthetic surface at this ground, and both of their wins over Cape Verde came in Monrovia, but the later of them is 15 years old and Cape Verde’s own record of conceding in every qualifier gives the hosts a route to one goal, which is why 1-2 is a better call than a repeat of the four-goal margin.

A Cape Verde win would lift them to six points, which only equals Rwanda’s tally if the Amavubi lose to Mali in Kigali on the same evening, so Bettencourt’s side cannot treat the second leg as a formality.

A trio of former Scottish Premiership stars are set to lose the manager who took them to the EFL Championship as part of the club’s massive summer revamp.

Scotland internationals Stephen Welsh and Ross Stewart both made Bosman free transfer moves to Swansea City in the summer from Celtic and Southampton respectively, while New Zealand forward Elijah Just joined them for a club-record fee of £6million from Motherwell following a stunning debut campaign at Fir Park.

However, the trio are set to see highly rated head coach Vitor Matos complete a shock exit from the club just three months after they arrived in South Wales, with the Portuguese boss remarked to be edging closer to a move that would see him appointed by Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg, who are expected to sack current manager Hugo Oliveira, after a run of five defeats in six matches.

Transformed under Matos since his arrival last November, the 38-year-old has enjoyed a strong start to the newly introduced campaign and has the second-tier side just three points from the automatic promotion spots in the English second tier, with eight wins in the opening 15 league matches.

It has been revealed that the move will come as a major blow for former Celtic and Motherwell centre-back Welsh. A regular starter under Matos since his summer arrival, he credited the former Marítimo boss as a key reason behind his maiden call-up to the Scotland senior squad in September.

A revelation on loan to Motherwell last season under Jens Berthel Askou, the 26-year-old was prized away by Swansea in the summer when his contract at Celtic expired in June. Detailing the reasons for moving across the border, Welsh specifically credited the impact of Matos on his decision.

According to recent reports, “They made it clear that they really wanted me,” remarked Welsh upon his arrival. “With the way the head coach spoke about the club, the environment he wants to create and the way he wants to play; it was a no-brainer. The Championship is a brilliant division, and one I am excited to be playing my football in and challenging myself in. I have experience but I am also young enough to be ready for a new opportunity and a new chapter in my career.”.

Meanwhile, former Ross County forward Stewart has found the net once in five games for Swansea, while Welsh’s former Motherwell teammate Just has started eight league games for his newly introduced side, assisting one in the 3-1 win over Burnley in September.

According to recent reports, despite his side’s strong start to the EFL Championship campaign, though, Matos looks destined to leave for France, with a switch to the western bank of the Rhine River, with several reports claiming a deal has been agreed for him to become the new Strasbourg head coach. He is expected to sign a deal until the summer of 2028, with a club option for an additional year through 2029.

The expected appointment will see him become Les Bleus' third manager in under a year after Gary O’Neil left to join Ipswich Town just four months after his appointment at Stade de la Meinau. His replacement, the aforementioned Oliveira, has been in charge for just 10 games.

‘Predictable, mutual, unfair’ - A brief history of Brighton’s sacked managers

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • So the current worst kept secret in football is out.
  • I recall being at the Amex on Easter Monday 2014, in the period of about 15 minutes I and four others in our party of ten that day received a forwarded text stating that David Moyes would be sacked as Manchester United manager the following morning, Tuesday 22nd April, and he was!
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So the current worst kept secret in football is out. Michael Carrick is no more at Old Trafford, it’s actually not United’s first rodeo in this footballing genre.

I recall being at the Amex on Easter Monday 2014, in the period of about 15 minutes I and four others in our party of ten that day received a forwarded text stating that David Moyes would be sacked as Manchester United manager the following morning, Tuesday 22nd April, and he was!

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It has been revealed that sackings are, unfortunately part and parcel of football. In my time following the Albion, we’ve had dismissals that have been predictable, justified, unfair and even a tad bizarre.

My first was Pat Saward in October 1973. I didn’t know much about, but in researching my book a couple of years ago, it was clear that once the ultra ambitious Albion chairman Mike Bamber got a sniff he might be able to rock the football world and bring Brian Clough to the Goldstone, dear old Pat was a dead man walking.

We then didn’t get another sacking for nearly a decade, and then it was all decided on the doorsteps of Sussex.

Sources indicate that mike Bailey had got the club it’s highest ever league finish, 13th in 81/82. But he was building from the back and at times the football wasn’t that exciting. Crowds dipped below the all important break even 15,000, and when fans were questioned by the lottery sellers on their weekly rounds, the word ‘boring’ was predominant and Bailey was out.

All these years later, I still believe the decision was a tad unfair and short sighted, but also one of those classic Brighton and Hove Albion sliding door moments.

Albion legend Steve Foster recently told me, whilst we probably wouldn’t have got to the 1983 Cup Final, we wouldn’t have got relegated and in time, Bailey could have turned us into a consistently top ten side, regularly challenging for Europe.

Bailey’s successor, Jimmy Melia, was almost in a footballing Sword of Damocles situation. Initially a caretaker boss, within a month the Albion embarked on an FA Cup campaign. With Bamber effectively waiting to wield the axe the Monday after the Albion were knocked out, but they weren’t. Melia, with his white dancing shoes took the Albion to Wembley but also rock bottom of the First Division and relegation!

Chris Cattlin was the next cab on the rank, his near three year tender, on a limited budget saw the Albion compete and again, like Bailey, given time, and funding, who knows what he could have achieved?

But he was unceremoniously dismissed at the end of the 85/86 season, but took the Albion to court for unfair dismissal, which resulted in his final victory at the club.

In a recent development, the returning Alan Mullery, another Goldstone legend, in the summer of 1986, was purely cosmetic. Replacing the popular Cattlin with the equally popular Mullery, saw a spike in season ticket sales, and not a lot more.

Mullery was a patsy, disgracefully treated when sacked in January 1987 for almost laughable reasons with the Albion in 13th.

A wretched run under new boss Barry Lloyd followed, with, as with the Division One exit in 1983, the Albion were relegated to the old Third Division in 22nd place in the division.

Recent findings suggest that yet we had to wait another nine years for another dismissal. Lloyd had left by mutual consent in December 1993, but in December 1996, with the cash strapped and soon to be homeless Albion in 92nd place in the Football League, Jimmy Case was unsurprisingly axed.

As was his successor, Steve Gritt, despite working a footballing miracle and keeping Albion in the league, he was gone in early 1998, again unjust, more about finance than football.

Exiled at Gillingham, crowds nowhere near break even, a massive shot in the arm was required, and that came in the shape of another returning legend (pattern forming) Brian Horton.

Jeff Wood, a genuinely nice guy, was in the wrong place at the wrong time Albion wise in 1999, as was Martin Hinshelwood in 2002.

Full disclosure, I’m in the privileged position to call a number of ex Albion bosses friends, and Mark McGhee is firmly in that catergory. His dismissal in September 2006, is another that sticks in the craw.

It has been revealed that I do however still have a degree of sympathy in the bigger picture. At the time, Dick Knight, chasing our collective Falmer dream, was juggling all the balls whilst protecting his own.

Dean Wilkins, still in my opinion technically one of the best coaches the club has ever had, was both a safe pair of hands but a far cheaper option whilst the battle for the stadium went on, tellingly though however he has never worked as a manager since he departed the club in 2008.

I still believe that Mark McGhee would have mounted a promotion challenge to get us back in the Championship.

With the greatest respect in my opinion Albion wise Russel Slade still remains an irrelevance, only doing the job that Micky Adams would have done had he not resigned in February 2009.

Which brings us on to Gus Poyet, a footballing firework, it was great whilst it lasted, but it was what it was, and given off field working relationships, or lack of them, it was never going to last.

But to clarify Gus was not sacked live in the BBC, he was fully aware of the situation and his subsequent reaction was as genuine as American Wrestling!

But he still gave us some great memories, which will never be forgotten.

Industry observers note that chris Hughton’s sacking in 2019, was another exit, which leaves a bad taste. It could have been handled so much better. Like the Moyes text of 2014, I was told that Graham Potter was coming in 40 minutes before Hughton kicked off what was to be his final Albion game. Yet he was interviewed by Richie Reynolds on the pitch at the end about his hopes for the next season!

Potter, could and should have been sacked at least one or two occasions, but a crumb of comfort was the £20 million Chelsea gave us for his services, it truly is a funny old game.

So was Roberto De Zerbi sacked in May 2024, or merely his contract not renewed?

I still love his time as Albion manager, like Gus and others some amazing memories, but unfortunately there are boundaries and as soon as that microphone went under his nose in Rome with the apparent diatribe against Tony Bloom there was only going to be one outcome.

In a recent development, which brings us around to Fab. Yes many, myself included, have embarked on the ‘Hurzeler Hokey Cokey’, but given the Albion’s current fortunes that’s well and truly parked.

You can never say never following the Albion but I think it’s a fairly safe bet there won’t be another Amex sacking anytime soon!

  • Jordan and Australia will face off in a rare November international friendly at Suheim Bin Hamad Stadium in Doha on Tuesday.
  • The home side are striving for consistency following their group-stage exit from the 2026 World Cup, while Australia will be looking to make it back-to-back away victories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 08:05.

Jordan and Australia will face off in a rare November international friendly at Suheim Bin Hamad Stadium in Doha on Tuesday.

The home side are striving for consistency following their group-stage exit from the 2026 World Cup, while Australia will be looking to make it back-to-back away victories.

Jordan may have fallen short of the group-stage hurdle at their first-ever World Cup, but they still produced some memorable moments for their supporters.

Despite suffering a 3-1 defeat to Austria in their opening game, Ali Olwan's stunning strike remains fresh in the memory.

Jordan failed to win either of their remaining matches against Algeria and Argentina, but they showed no shortage of fighting spirit before their World Cup campaign came to an end.

Badou Zaki's side are now without a win in their last 10 matches and have recorded two draws since the tournament.

The Chivalrous Ones played out a 1-1 draw against Syria in their first match after the World Cup in September before being held to a goalless stalemate by Venezuela in October, extending their winless run through two underwhelming friendlies.

In contrast, Australia enjoyed a memorable tournament, reaching the knockout stages despite being drawn in a difficult group.

Tony Popovic's side stunned many with a 2-0 victory over a strong Turkey outfit in their opening match.

They subsequently lost 2-0 to the USA, but a goalless draw was enough to secure their passage into the knockout rounds, where they suffered a 4-2 penalty shootout defeat to Egypt after the match finished 1-1 in normal time.

Australia faced Brazil twice in international friendlies after the World Cup, drawing 1-1 in the first encounter before losing 4-2 in the return fixture.

However, they head into this contest with renewed confidence after thrashing Qatar 3-0 earlier this week, with all three goals arriving in the first half.

Zaki has a fully fit squad at his disposal, and it will be interesting to see which combination he opts for.

Abdallah Al-Fakhouri could retain his place in goal, although Alec Samir featured in the 1-1 draw against Syria.

World Cup hero Mousa Al-Tamari is expected to lead the attack alongside Olwan and veteran forward Mahmoud Al-Mardi.

Australia, meanwhile, are missing several key players, with Cameron Burgess ruled out by a cruciate ligament injury and Jordan Bos also sidelined with a knee problem.

The Socceroos are also without skipper Mathew Ryan and fellow veterans Jackson Irvine and Milos Degenek, plus midfielder Aiden O'Neill, but it unclear whether they made themselves unavailable for safety reasons.

Diesel Herrington, Thomas Waddingham and Sam Klein are fresh call-ups, while striker Kusini Yengi joins brother Tete Yengi, while goalkeepers Joe Gauci and Tom Glover have been recalled.

Jordan possible starting lineup:.

Al-Fakhouri; Badawi, Nasib, Rousan, Taha; Sadeh, Al-Rawabdeh, Qashi; Tamari, Olwan, Al-Mardi.

Australia possible starting lineup:.

Beach; Kasey Bos, Herrington, Souttar, Circati, Italiano; McGree, Metcalfe, Okon-Engstler; Irankunda, Yengi.

Jordan will be desperate to secure their first victory since 2025 and should fancy their chances against an Australian side missing several key players. However, the visitors will be keen to end the international break unbeaten, and we expect an entertaining contest to finish level.

Brighton star Mats Wieffer admits he felt ‘restricted’ in the full back role as he targets a regular spot in central midfield.

The Dutch international joined Brighton as a midfielder for around £25m in 2024 but often played as a reluctant right full back.

It's a position Wieffer adapted to pretty well but now the former Feyenoord man is keen to make an impact in his preferred central midfield role.

Ferdi Kadioglu and Costinha are now the recognised right backs at Brighton, which means Wieffer can now compete for midfield minutes, alongside the likes of Pascal Gross, Yasin Ayari, Jack Hinshelwood, Diego Gomez and Chema Andres, who has impressed since his summer arrival.

Chema joined for around £20m from VfB Stuttgart and Wieffer feels they operate in a similar position.

Wieffer - who is fit once again following a recent knee injury - remarked to the club website: "I can still play both, but I'm happy to play in midfield.

"Now I need to keep the rhythm, train hard, and get all the principles there, because for the last two seasons I was more focused on full-back.

“I think Chema [Andres] and I are a little bit similar, but the rest are a little bit different. If I have to compare myself, I'm more like Chema than the others.”.

Industry observers note that he added: “You're always happy to play, but overall I prefer midfield because I've always done it. As a full-back, you're a little bit restricted, and I think I'm a better player as a midfielder overall.

Recent findings suggest that “But last season went really well, and he always told me I was playing well and the system suited me. The stats were good, which gave me confidence that he put me in the starting XI.

“The team and playing are always the most important things for me. In the end I'm happy, but if I could choose I would play in midfield.”.

Brighton are second in the table and resume Premier league action after the international break at Hull City.

It's been an impressive start to the season as Brighton have 22 points from 10 matches and are the division's leading scorers.

Wieffer stated: “Last season we had the same kind of principles we have now, but this season we are doing it every game.

“When everybody sees that the things we train are working it gives the feeling that if we keep doing this it will pay off in points.

Sources indicate that “Most importantly, it's because of the things we do like the pressing. Last season we didn't do it every game.

“In the bigger games we were always there but sometimes in the games we thought we needed to win it was a little bit less and opponents punished us.

“That was frustrating - getting points from a bigger team and then dropping points against a team we thought we were equals with.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 01:18.
  • Fighting for a chance at survival in UEFA Nations League B, Poland will welcome Group B4 winners Sweden to Tarczynski Arena on Tuesday.
  • The Eagles are under pressure, though the Blue and Yellow have already clinched top spot and could be caught off guard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 01:18.

Fighting for a chance at survival in UEFA Nations League B, Poland will welcome Group B4 winners Sweden to Tarczynski Arena on Tuesday.

The Eagles are under pressure, though the Blue and Yellow have already clinched top spot and could be caught off guard.

Jan Urban's Poland have endured a dire campaign so far, and the best they can hope for at this stage is to qualify for the League B/C playoffs.

The Eagles only required a draw against Romania last time out to secure a place in an inter-division showdown, but they were beaten 2-1 in Bucharest on Saturday.

That defeat has left Urban's side third in Group B4 with four points to their name, just one clear of Romania ahead of the final matchday.

Knowing that victory for their rivals could force them into the automatic relegation spot, Poland will be fearing a clash against in-form Sweden, especially after losing three of their last four outings.

However, the hosts will take heart from the fact they are unbeaten on home soil during this group stage, having drawn 0-0 with Bosnia-Herzegovina on September 25, before thrashing Romania 6-0 a week later.

Meanwhile, Graham Potter's Sweden are yet to taste defeat in Group B4, and are set to play League A football next term following an excellent campaign.

The Blue and Yellow held on to beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-2 on Saturday, racing into a three-goal lead courtesy of a fifth-minute opener from Borussia Dortmund's Daniel Svensson and a pair of penalties from Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres, but conceded twice in a tense second half.

That performance fits Sweden's pattern, considering they have scored in the first 20 minutes during six of their last seven Nations League clashes, while 13 of their past 15 matches have seen both sides find the back of the net.

Regardless, securing their fourth win in five games has Potter's men top of the group with 13 points, five clear of the second-placed Dragons and nine above third-placed Poland.

The Blue and Yellow may no longer be under pressure, but they will be keen to end on a positive note, and having won eight of their last nine meetings with Poland, supporters will be looking forward to another triumph on Tuesday.

Poland will be without Porto centre-back Jakub Kiwior, who is suspended due to accumulating yellow cards, while Aston Villa right-back Matty Cash is a doubt with a leg problem and goalkeeper Kamil Grabara is sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury.

In their absence, Kacper Potulski could be joined by Tomasz Kedziora at the heart of the hosts' defence, flanked by Arkadiusz Pyrka and Oskar Kubiak at full-back in front of shot-stopper Bartlomiej Dragowski.

Elsewhere, Inter Milan midfielder Piotr Zielinski is unavailable due to illness, though Sebastian Szymanski and Wiktor Nowak should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

As for Sweden, they are missing Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall (knee) and Lech Poznan winger Patrik Walemark (muscle).

With that in mind, expect to see Fulham's Hugo Larsson and Brighton and Hove Albion's Yasin Ayari line up in midfield, while Anthony Elanga and Sebastian Nanasi provide width.

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak will partner Viktor Gyokeres up top on Tuesday, with the latter hoping to add to his brace from last time out.

Poland possible starting lineup:.

Dragowski; Pyrka, Potulski, Kedziora, Kubiak; Regula, Szymanski, Nowak, Zalewski; Lewandowski, Swiderski.

Sweden possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Svensson, Lagerbielke, Lindelof, Gudmundsson; Elanga, Larsson, Ayari, Nanasi; Gyokeres, Isak.

Poland are sure to be feeling the pressure from Romania on Tuesday, and they will be keen to confirm their place in the playoffs.

However, Sweden have dominated the head-to-head clashes between these nations, and are likely to continue that trend in midweek.

Arsenal forward Christos Tzolis has avoided serious injury despite feeling discomfort after Greece's game against the Netherlands, the latest report has revealed.

The Gunners will resume their quest for the Premier League title on Saturday, when they take on Newcastle United in matchweek 11.

However, there are fears that Mikel Arteta's squad may be weakened further ahead of that clash at St James' Park.

Winger Tzolis has already suffered a hamstring injury this season, missing four league matches, but he was taken off in the 73rd minute of Greece's clash with the Netherlands on Friday.

Journalist Dimitris Manakos has revealed that the winger had an MRI scan due to discomfort, though he has not suffered a serious injury and has not been ruled out of Monday's match against Serbia.

While there is no suggestion that Tzolis will miss Saturday's game for Arsenal, it would not be surprising if he started on the bench in order to avoid an injury occurring.

The Gunners will likely start Kai Havertz as a striker, while Noni Madueke is also set to feature on the right side of attack.

Other than Tzolis, there is no natural left-winger in the squad, and that could force Arteta to select Eberechi Eze for that flank.

Tzolis has not scored for the Gunners this season, and while he has registered four assists, two came in the Community Shield.

The Greek international's performances arguably do not merit a place in the team, but Arsenal may not have a better option on the left.

Madueke can play on both flanks, though he has been forced to fill in for Bukayo Saka on the right, while Eze has consistently failed to impress out wide.

Arsenal should not be in a position where they have to rely on Tzolis, and the fact Arteta does not have an elite wide player on the left is a damning indictment of the club's transfer policy in recent years.
