📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that that's how widely-respected Spanish sports newspaper Marca described La Roja's rivalry with England following the Three Lions' stunning Sunday-best victory at the Metropolitano. High praise indeed.

That it is becoming one of the most absorbing and significant in world football is surely beyond doubt now.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In a recent development, in terms of beating the world champions, England have been here before. Back in November 2011, a screamer from Frank Lampard secured a Wembley victory against the feted Spanish, who were also European Championship holders at the same time.

Recent findings suggest that this felt different. On that aforesaid occasion, England prevailed following a backs-to-the-wall performance which saw them pinned back in their own half for long spells against dominant opponents. They converted one of just two chances that came their way.

By contrast, Sunday saw those in white subjugate Spain with an elite showing.

Certainly for 65 to 70 minutes, the hosts' much-vaunted midfield—Arsenal duo Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, alongside Fabián Ruiz and Alex Baena—were suffocated by England's high press.

It has been revealed that it was an intense game plan executed 'with the precision of a master tailor' in the words of Marca. Ruiz and Merino both got the hook at half-time.

The narrative only changed when Elliot Anderson received his marching orders.

It has been revealed that the hosts roared back and things became undeniably hairy in the final quarter. But unlike against Argentina in Atlanta in July, Thomas Tuchel's substitutions did not see England adopt a defensive straitjacket.

Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin came on as the visitors focused on staying higher up the pitch, if at all possible, amid serious late pressure from Spain.

It has been revealed that it ended in a merited 3-2 win for the English. In three of the last four meetings between these two, a team has triumphed by the odd goal in five.

England triumphed by the same scoreline and in similar fashion to their previous visit to Spain back in October 2018 - in another Nations League encounter played out in Seville, this time. Again, they achieved success by being proactive as opposed to parking the bus.

Fabulous counter-attacking strikes from Raheem Sterling (2) and Marcus Rashford put the visitors 3-0 up to silence the Spanish hordes. It was the prelude to a strong home fightback in the second half, but no victory.

On this occasion, England's physical and tactical dominance was even more sustained and their third goal, scored by Ben White on 57 minutes, finished off a move of the highest order.

For too long in the past, certainly before that 2018 occasion in Seville, England had been cowed on their visits to Spain. In their previous four matches, all defeats, they failed to score. Ever since Gary Lineker, then at Barcelona, struck all four goals in a stunner at Madrid's Bernebeu Stadium in February 1987.

England have now regained the full respect of international football's undoubted success story of the current century. The team who, alongside France, are the current benchmark for all other nations.

Sunday night was undeniably sweetened by the fact that Spain relinquished their magnificent 44-game unbeaten sequence in the process.

That run included a 2-1 win over England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin and this summer’s World Cup.

Spain's previous defeat was back in March 2023 against Scotland in Glasgow.

On an evening when the usual suspects came to the party in the shape of Jude Bellingham, whose pass for White's goal was delectable and Harry Kane, others also accepted their invites.

What a night for Leeds's James Trafford for instance. His fantastic double save late on to deny Fer Lopez and Aymeric Laporte announced his arrival on the world stage.

It presents Tuchel with a genuine headache - a welcome one, that mentioned - regarding who will be his bonafide No 1 in 2027.

According to recent reports, the battle between Trafford and Jordan Pickford is now a proper fight. It's not quite Peter Shilton versus Ray Clemence levels in the 1970s and early 80s just yet, but it might be heading in that direction. Tellingly, Trafford started both Nations League games against Spain, as opposed to his Everton rival.

Remember, remember the month of November? England will.

Sunday's success was a statement win of the ilk of 2015 when they beat the French 2-0 at Wembley and a decade earlier, in the same month, when a late brace from Michael Owen saw them triumph 3-2 against bitter foes Argentina, in Geneva of all places. Let's hope on this occasion, they build on it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 02:26.

Romania will be battling for a chance at avoiding relegation from UEFA Nations League B on Tuesday, when they travel to face Bosnia-Herzegovina at Stadion Bilino Polje.

The Dragons have already secured second in Group B4, and are up against a Tricolorii team that need to win.

Sergej Barbarez's Bosnia-Herzegovina will be hoping to end their group stage on a high note after nailing down a spot in the League A/B playoffs.

The Dragons were downed 3-2 by group winners Sweden on Saturday, conceding three first-half goals before falling agonisingly short of a comeback with two strikes of their own in the second period.

In fairness to Barbarez's side, that loss was their first of this Nations League campaign following two draws and two wins, including a 4-2 triumph over Tuesday's opponents on September 28.

Heading into this clash, Bosnia-Herzegovina are second with eight points - five behind Sweden but four clear of third-placed Poland - and securing the runners-up spot has presented the Dragons with a shot at promotion to League A.

Another victory in midweek could give the team a boost ahead of their playoff, and fans will be expecting a positive result, given that Barbarez's men have not suffered back-to-back defeats since November 2024.

Meanwhile, Gheorghe Hagi's Romania have delivered a dire campaign so far, but escaping with all three points on Saturday has given them a glimmer of hope.

The Tricolorii lost each of their first four Nations League fixtures this term, conceding 13 goals while scoring just three in the process, and seemed doomed to relegation to League C.

However, a shock 2-1 victory over Poland last time out has placed Group B4's bottom side just one point behind the third-placed Eagles in the League B/C playoff spot.

Due to their 6-0 thrashing by Poland on October 2, Romania must beat Bosnia-Herzegovina while hoping that their rivals drop points to Sweden in order to avoid automatic demotion.

That being noted, the Tricolorii have not come out on top in any of their eight away matches since hammering San Marino 5-1 in March 2025, losing six times and drawing twice.

Bosnia-Herzegovina Nations League form:.

Bosnia-Herzegovina have doubts about the readiness of striker Haris Tabakovic, who was forced off just 39 minutes into the clash against Sweden due to a knee injury.

If the Red Bull Salzburg man is unavailable, then Ermedin Demirovic could be joined by Ermin Mahmic up front on Tuesday, supported from out wide by Esmir Bajraktarevic and Kerim Alajbegovic.

At the opposite end of the pitch, centre-back Dennis Hadzikadunic is sidelined with a muscle injury, so Nikola Katic and Stjepan Radeljic should start at the heart of Barbarez's defence.

As for Romania, they are missing midfielder Tudor Baluta, who is suspended for accumulating yellow cards, so Alexandru Cicaldau, Vladimir Screciu and Vlad Dragomir are likely to operate in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, Florinel Coman and Dennis Man look set to lead the line once again on Tuesday, aided in attack by Alanyaspor's Ianis Hagi.

Bosnia-Herzegovina possible starting lineup:.

Zlomislic; Dedic, Katic, Radeljic, Kolasinac; Bajraktarevic, Basic, Gigovic, Alajbegovic; Mahmic, Demirovic.

Romania possible starting lineup:.

Hindrich; Ratiu, Coubis, Dragusin, Eissat; Cicaldau, Screciu, Dragomir; Hagi; Coman, Man.

Bosnia-Herzegovina may have lost to Sweden at the weekend, but they have proven resilient across this Nations League campaign and will be seen as overwhelming favourites on Tuesday.

Romania have struggled in League B, and given their dire away form - not to mention their four defeats this term - it would be surprising to see the visitors avoid another loss.

Among them is the rise to prominence of defender Sean Roughan, who is starting to show the form which alerted Town to his potential during his yeoman service at Lincoln City.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Irishman has impressed after casting aside an untimely thigh injury sustained in the club's opening game of the season in early August, the Carabao Cup tie against Preston North End.

Roughan, 23, has not looked back since being restored to the starting line-up for the game at Plymouth Argyle on October 17.

The Dubliner was excellent in the 2-0 victory at a high-flying competitor at the top end of the third tier, after stepping in for the injured Murray Wallace, and has started the club's last five league matches.

That spell, in which Town have been unbeaten, has seen Martin Drury's side pick up an eye-catching 13 points from a possible 15 ahead of Saturday's mouth-watering test against another form side in Leicester City, who visit the Accu Stadium.

Along the way, Roughan also laid a ghost to rest.

After a very tough appointment at Bradford City last autumn - when Town were humbled 3-1—he played an instrumental part in the visitors turning things around at Valley Parade this season in a 3-0 victory on Hallowe'en.

Head coach Drury, whose side are three-quarters of the way through a run of four successive home games in all competitions, said: "I've really been impressed by Sean's mentality this season.

Sources indicate that "He's been out injured and he's missed some time. He's come back into the team. I think he's showing more leadership and he's more vocal and he's competing.

"It was a tough game at Bradford because they play long balls and diagonal balls and you're constantly fighting and scrapping and it's not a clean game. I felt his mentality was strong throughout that game and it has been in other games.

"So a lot of credit needs to go to Sean and the medical and performance staff for the way they brought him back.".

#14290. Industry News: Move over BMI: latest obesity definition is better for predicting your health

Industry News: Move over BMI: latest obesity definition is better for predicting your health

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A study suggests that people are being misdiagnosed as having obesity with a metric known as the body mass index (BMI).Credit: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP/Getty.
  • Clinicians have debated for years whether body mass index (BMI) — a metric derived from a person’s height and weight — is the best way to define and diagnose obesity.
  • New obesity definition sidelines BMI to focus on health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A study suggests that people are being misdiagnosed as having obesity with a metric known as the body mass index (BMI).Credit: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP/Getty.

Clinicians have debated for years whether body mass index (BMI) — a metric derived from a person’s height and weight — is the best way to define and diagnose obesity. Now, an approach that measures waist circumference and focuses more closely on excess body fat has proved to be better than BMI at predicting a person’s risk of death.

New obesity definition sidelines BMI to focus on health.

New obesity definition sidelines BMI to focus on health.

It has been revealed that an analysis of data collected from more than 800,000 individuals found that using BMI to diagnose obesity failed to identify a considerable proportion of people with elevated health risks caused by excess body fat. The study was published today in Nature1.

Sources indicate that physicians know that BMI — calculated by dividing a person’s weight by the square of their height — doesn’t accurately reflect body composition. For example, a muscular person might have an elevated BMI but have little body fat. The latest study “reinforces that BMI is not a good measure of obesity at the individual level and is not good in terms of predicting who is going to develop cardiometabolic disease in the long term”, says Cátia Martins, an obesity researcher at the University of Alabama at Birmingham.

But given how simple it is to calculate BMI, it remains the most widely used tool to classify obesity.

A person is usually diagnosed with obesity if they have a BMI of 30 or higher. The approach presented in the study — called the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, or CAD-obesity — goes beyond BMI, combining it with measures, such as waist circumference, that are linked to excess body fat. Physicians know that when fat tissue is preferentially stored in the abdominal area, it is associated with more negative health consequences than when it’s stored elsewhere, Martins says.

Why BMI is flawed — and how to redefine obesity.

Why BMI is flawed — and how to redefine obesity.

Under the CAD-obesity system2, first proposed last year, people with obesity who also have at least one of 18 specific health problems — including heart failure and sleep apnoea — are classified as having ‘clinical obesity’. This indicates that excess fat is harming their organs and tissues. Those with obesity but none of these health problems are classified as having ‘preclinical obesity’, in which a person has excess fat but their organs are functioning normally.

“We did not know until now whether or not this fresh framework had implications in the real world and a prognostic value,” says Francesco Rubino, a weight-loss surgeon at King’s College London who led the effort to create the system and is a co-author of the Nature paper.

But Rubino and his colleagues proved the system’s worth by examining medical records from four large groups of people in China, Spain, the United Kingdom and the United States. They used data from three of those cohorts, in which more than 50,000 deaths occurred over up to 15 years, to determine whether BMI or the CAD-obesity system was a better indicator of elevated mortality risk.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03636-5.

Breaking: Chile vs Colombia - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 16 Nov 2026 04:16.
  • Fresh off the first of two consecutive meetings on Saturday, Chile and Colombia will meet for another international friendly and their final games of 2026 on Tuesday in Santiago.
  • Tuesday's hosts won the reverse fixture 1-0 away from home, extending their unbeaten streak against Chile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 16 Nov 2026 04:16.

Fresh off the first of two consecutive meetings on Saturday, Chile and Colombia will meet for another international friendly and their final games of 2026 on Tuesday in Santiago.

Tuesday's hosts won the reverse fixture 1-0 away from home, extending their unbeaten streak against Chile.

Chile return to action for their final game of the year on Tuesday aiming to bow out on a positive note after a tough year.

La Roja faced no competitive action in 2026, having fallen short in South American World Cup qualifying last year, meaning they have played just eight times prior to Tuesday's upcoming fixture, losing five and winning three of those.

Nicolas Cordova's team did end the September and October international break with a 2-0 victory over Mexico, thanks to goals from Maximiliano Gutierrez and Vicente Pizarro, but they failed to carry that into the final break of the term, falling short against Colombia again away from home last Saturday.

A trip to Cali ended in a 1-0 loss for La Roja, their fifth defeat in seven games while failing to score for a second time and making it a sixth game against Colombia without a win since a 2019 Copa America penalty shootout triumph.

Now taking their turn to have home advantage for the reverse fixture in Santiago, Chile will set out to end the year with a victory before looking forward and aiming to build in the fresh year.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip to Santiago aiming to round off their positive year with a double over Chile.

Colombia's 2026 will be remembered for a creditable showing at the World Cup in USA, Mexico and Canada, as La Tricolor topped their group on seven points with two wins and a draw against Portugal.

They would then get past Ghana thanks to Jhon Arias's goal, before falling just short at the hands of Switzerland in the round of 16, losing a penalty shootout after a goalless draw.

In four friendlies since, Nestor Lorenzo's team have won twice, firstly ending the September and October break by beating Peru 2-0 before they beat Chile in Cali on Saturday with a first-half own goal from Guillermo Maripan making the difference.

Now on seven wins in 13 games in the calendar year, Colombia head to Chile looking to make it a perfect final break of 2026 and record another victory.

Colombia form (all competitions):.

Nicolas Cordova has a relatively inexperienced Chile squad for the November friendlies, with defenders Paulo Diaz and Benjamin Kuscevic and Paulo Diaz missing out while key midfielder Marcelino Nunez is also not involved.

Ben Brereton Diaz boasts the most experience in a young attacking unit, with 46 caps and 10 international goals to his name, and he may come in from the outset after a substitute appearance in the last game.

That is after Gutierrez, Gonzalo Tapia and Crystal Palace prospect Dario Osorio started in a front three in Colombia, while Rodrigo Echeverria, one of just four players aged above 30 years old, should continue in midfield alongside Vicente Pizarro.

Colombia have also seen plenty of change in their squad, particularly since the World Cup, with James Rodriguez, Juan Quintero and David Ospina retiring while Juan Cuadrado, Santiago Arias, Yerry Mina, Richard Rios and Jhon Duran are also not involved.

Arguably the most notable omission is injured Bayern Munich winger Luis Diaz, leaving La Tricolor light and inexperienced up top.

The line should again be led by Luis Suarez, who has eight goals in 21 caps and 13 in 15 appearances across the Primeira Liga and Champions League for Sporting Lisbon, while a fresh look squad is headlined by the likes of Daniel Munoz, Davinson Sanchez and Jefferson Lerma.

Chile possible starting lineup:.

Vigouroux; Villagra, Maripan, Ulloa; Loyola, Echeverria, Pizarro, Suazo; Osorio, Brereton Diaz, Gutierrez.

Colombia possible starting lineup:.

Vargas; Munoz, Sanchez, Lucumi, Velasquez; Duran, Puerta, Lerma, Perea; Suarez, Arias.

Given both sides' relatively limited options at the top end of the pitch, we anticipate another low-scoring encounter on Tuesday and give the edge to the visitors to complete a double over Chile.
